ONE of the three cases is proven end to end and two are unit tests only; the split matters more than the total, and ADR 0005 records the judgment behind it. PROVEN END TO END on the installed shell (proof 8, using the issue's numbering): case 2, the request the runner destroyed because its bounded buffer was full. A real agent the runner spawned fired 200 brokered requests past a buffer of 64 and the shell's own broker loop drained, recorded and rendered them - 200 sent, 64 adjudicated, 136 dropped, identical in all three runs, so it is a bound being hit rather than a race. 8d is the load-bearing check: audit rows plus dropped requests may not exceed what the agent actually sent, which is exactly what a synthesised row would do, and a build that faked a plausible decision would pass every other check in the file and fail that one. 8e asserts the lapse carries no operation, decision or refusal; 8f asserts the rendered sentence names no operation either. UNIT TESTS ONLY: case 1 (DASH was closed) and case 3 (the answer DASH could not confirm was delivered). The issue's own account of case 3 was wrong and is corrected in ADR 0005: an undeliverable answer does not leave no trace, because lib/broker/execute.ts audits on every path before the answer travels, so the row already exists and overstates - it became a delivered column on the audit row rather than a second population of near-misses. issues.note: THE RUN HAPPENED AND IT WAS GREEN. PROVEN BY THE ATTENDED REAL-GOOGLE RUN OF 2026-08-07 20:25-20:28Z, WHICH PASSED ALL SIXTEEN CHECKS G0a-G16 against https://gmail.googleapis.com with no loopback provider in force. Full log and record on MAR-468. The checks that carry the most: G2/G3 a real consent stored as a refresh token in Windows Credential Manager (DPAPI); G4 the three-party intersection over a real credential granting exactly gmail.draft.create, gmail.search and gmail.message.read with no missing and no unused scopes; G5 the wider-permission sentence admitting Google has no drafts-only permission; G8b the projection over REAL Gmail MIME, which ADR 0002 amendment 3 named the single most likely thing to be wrong - projected_fields carried from_address beside the raw from, raw_from_had_display_name true and from_address_is_bare true, which is MAR-523's parse working against a real display-name sender; G9/G10 Gmail accepting the composed reply (draft id r2827601834087138528) and filing it against the same thread the read came from (19fd86d6d726145f both sides); G11 both send attempts refused unknown_operation against a credential that really carries gmail.compose; G12a a CRLF-carrying recipient refused invalid_input before any request reached Google; G13 no Google token observable in the agent process or its environment; G15a Google accepting the revocation and G15b the agent's very next poll refused as revoked rather than as a generic failure, with allowed_before_revoked true - the ordering MAR-523 established by construction rather than by winning a race; G16 the operator inspecting the real draft in Gmail (own address in From, one recipient, no Bcc) and deleting it. The preflight ADOPTED a credentialed runner from the failed 20:14Z attempt rather than demanding a restart, which is MAR-520's fix working in the field. Grant withdrawn at Google, vault copy deleted, draft deleted, nothing left running. THE FOUR QUALIFICATIONS THE RUNBOOK'S PROMOTION RULE REQUIRES, CARRIED HERE RATHER THAN CITED: (1) THE RUN IS DATED 2026-08-07 AND ITS TESTING-MODE GRANT EXPIRED OR EXPIRES 2026-08-14, SEVEN DAYS LATER, so this evidence has a shelf life and a later reader must not treat it as current without a fresh run. A public connection would require Google verification, and an annual independent CASA assessment if restricted-scope data ever transits a server; neither is proven by this run and neither is claimed. (3) G12b IS THE WEAKER HALF OF PROOF 7's 7n. Google cannot be made to serve a send endpoint and refuse it on command, so G12b reads DASH's own audit (6 rows, 0 allowed sends) where 7n reads a provider that would have answered. Proof 7 still owns the stronger statement, is NOT superseded and must not be deleted; G11 runs the other way - a send refused against a credential really carrying gmail.compose, which no loopback run can claim - so the two proofs are complementary. Everything about the broker, the projection, the write, the negatives, the audit and the revocation is UNTOUCHED - the run never reached a brokered call, and nothing here is evidence for or against any of it. MACHINE STATE: nothing to clean. No credential reached the vault, so the cleanup had nothing to revoke and no orphan grant exists at Google - confirmed absent from the account's third-party app list. No draft was created and no draft id was printed. THE LESSON THIS ISSUE'S OWN NOTE PREDICTED, pointed one level up: it said a runbook is not a run. A harness that builds is not a harness that runs either. Everything about this harness reachable without a consent screen HAD been validated - typecheck, esbuild bundle, node --check on the generated agent - and all three defects live strictly outside that set. PRIOR NOTE, still accurate about what was BUILT: What was built: scripts/google-proof/main.ts (an Electron main entry, checks G0a-G16), scripts/prove-google.mjs (builds and launches it) and docs/real-google-proof-runbook.md. The design decision that mattered was NOT writing it as a standalone script driving lib/broker/ directly, which is the cheap way. It boots the same shell through the same electron/smoke-identity.ts and electron/main.ts, writes to the same user-data directory, uses the same OS vault, adopts the same runner and spawns a real child speaking the same broker protocol - so the only variable between it and proof 7 is which server answers, plus the pre-consent summary window, which is a renderer surface and not on the path any provider request takes. There is therefore no substrate seam between the two proofs, only one check. That check is 7n: proof 7's harness SERVES Gmail's two send endpoints and answers them with success, which is what makes 'DASH never called a send endpoint' a statement about DASH rather than about a provider's willingness to refuse. Google cannot be made willing, so G12b reads broker_audit instead and is weaker in exactly that way - it would not distinguish a request DASH built and Google rejected from one DASH never built. The asymmetry runs both ways and is why neither proof is redundant: G11 refuses both send attempts against a credential Google would genuinely have honoured, which no loopback grant can model because that grant is a fixture the harness wrote itself. Both stay; proof 7 runs on every commit and this one runs when somebody is watching. G0b is the cheapest check and the one the whole record rests on - loopbackProofOrigin() must be null, or every check below would pass against the fake provider and the dated log would be a lie about which server answered; the run stops there if it fails. It cannot become a gate by construction, not by convention: scripts/prove-google.mjs exits before it builds anything if CI is set or no terminal is attached, and no package.json script names it (ADR 0004). pnpm verify does not run it and DOES typecheck it - tsconfig.json now includes scripts/google-proof - because a proof that rots silently between attended runs would be worse than none, and typechecking a file is not executing it. The write half creates a REAL draft in a REAL Drafts folder, said before the step and behind a typed confirmation; DASH has no operation that deletes a draft and this proof must not be the reason one gets built, so the operator deletes it in Gmail and confirms. The run ends by revoking at Google, which is also check G15b: the agent's next request must come back 'revoked' rather than as a generic failure, a MAR-446 acceptance criterion that until now had only ever been asked of a test server returning a hand-written invalid_grant. Regime when it is run: Testing mode with a named test user. Both scopes are RESTRICTED, a public connection needs Google verification, and restricted-scope data crossing a server needs an annual CASA assessment - none of which a Testing-mode run is evidence about. Testing-mode data-scope grants expire SEVEN DAYS after issue, so the record must carry its date. Evidence for this session, and it is evidence about the HARNESS rather than about Google - the attended proof itself is unexecuted: two full pnpm verify runs on Windows, both green, and the requirement they were run against is that verify still passes WITHOUT this proof in it. Each reported [state] valid with the 6 recorded drift warnings, typecheck clean, 62 test files / 1113 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, and 67 installed-shell proof checks with ZERO failures plus the one advisory note (6l, the live sources, which can never fail a release; all three answered, 456-604ms). 67 is unchanged from c6c3406 and that is correct: MAR-421 landed in between and added 9 unit tests and no installed proof, which is why the test count moved from 1104 to 1113 and the proof count did not. What varied between the two runs was the harness and not the product, and the first account of it written here was wrong in a way worth recording. Run 1's exit code did not appear when the run finished, because the smoke leaves the runner running on purpose and that detached process inherits the Tee-Object pipeline's stdout handle, which PowerShell waits on - so the pipeline stayed open with the log complete and locked. A DECISION, and nothing was implemented - lib/, electron/, runner/, contracts/ and .github/workflows/ are untouched by design, and so are orchestratekit-mcp and orchestratelab, which were read-only this session. ADR 0006 decides that the broker's reach ends at the machine DASH is installed on: a process DASH's own runner did not spawn gets no brokered credential, DASH will not operate a hosted token broker, and an agent that must run while DASH is closed holds its own credentials on the agent_managed path that already exists. That is option 3 for the broker and option 1 for the product, argued as one rule about one boundary rather than two decisions. THE FINDING THAT SHAPED IT: the rule is already enforced by the transport rather than by policy. Since MAR-430 the runner listens on a Unix socket or a Windows named pipe and never on a port, so there is no address an off-machine process could dial, and runner/server.ts keeps isLocalPeer only against a TCP listener that does not exist. What was missing is that nothing writes it down - which is why examples/gmail-meeting-assistant.manifest.v2.example.json can declare continues_when_dash_closed true beside two dash_managed connections, validate, and tell the user only afterwards as an ADR 0005 case-1 lapse row. A hosted broker was rejected on four costs and the shortest decides it: it would make ADR 0002 invariant 1 a rule again after amendment 1 spent a paragraph on why its being a FACT about where the code can run is what made the boundary worth having. The other three: what a user trusts changes category from installed software to an operator; revocation stops being locally checkable, which is proof 7n's lesson pointed at a receipt; and ADR 0002's own Google release path attaches an annual independent CASA assessment at an assessor-set fee the moment restricted-scope data crosses a server. Its receipt already fails the honesty test IN THE CODE: describeCustody's hosted_broker sentence is missing the clause its remote_mcp_server sibling has, and both ways of writing it are bad. ON THE CONTRACT QUESTION: continues_when_dash_closed is NOT sufficient and NO new field is needed. It asks a question about time where a grant needs one about place, and the shipped Gmail example disproves it directly - runtime.class local_process, locations.runtime.kind local, continues_when_dash_closed true. locations.runtime.kind already carries place, is required, and orchestratekit-mcp already emits it (runtimeLocationKind maps managed_worker/scheduled_job/workflow_platform to remote); it must not be the gate either, because it is the author's claim about a fact DASH observes directly by having spawned the process. So it drives copy, never a grant. ADR 0002 amendment 4 narrows the four sentences of 0002 that were written as universals - the Decision's first line and invariants 1, 3 and 5 - and records that invariant 6 keeps every word while stopping being reassuring about the mailbox. WHAT STOPS BEING PROVEN, named rather than discovered later: broker_audit stops being a complete answer to what has been done to an account, and this is NOT a fourth broker_lapses case because a lapse needs DASH to observe its own absence and DASH is uninvolved rather than absent; revocation stops being immediate for the connections most likely to matter; proof 7g has no analogue past the line, because on the unbrokered side the token IS in the agent's environment by design, so the honesty burden sits entirely on copy; and nothing about remote deployment can ever have a blocking gate under ADR 0004's rule, permanently rather than until somebody automates it. NOT FILED, named in the ADR's follow-ups instead because this session may not touch lib/: describeCustody's hosted_broker sentence should gain the clause its sibling has, since under this decision that value can only ever describe a third party's broker. Epic MAR-475; siblings MAR-477 (the MCP->DASH round-trip proof, whose seam this session re-verified field-for-field against both repositories), MAR-478 (deploy to a host, blocked by this) and MAR-479 (the opt-in LAB telemetry ADR). issues.note: MERGED to master in PR #44 (merge commit fb3f764) on 2026-08-06. The opening sentence this replaces said PLANNED and deliberately without a commit, which was true when written. Linear moves In Review -> In Progress rather than to Done, because In Review in this project means a PR is open and In Progress means merged-and-not-proven, which is what MAR-458, MAR-467, MAR-469, MAR-421, MAR-484 and MAR-497 all carry; the installed-shell evidence here is CI's own shell-smoke on the branch tip rather than a run this session executed, and promoting to proven on somebody else's prose is exactly the move this packet exists to prevent. PRIOR NOTE: Filed AFTER the fix rather than before it - the work arrived as a bug report against MAR-420 on master - and an issue written afterwards is a record rather than intent, which is why it says so. MAR-420's DensityScript sets data-density on document.documentElement before hydration, and app/layout.tsx renders <html>, so React hydrated it, found an attribute the build-time markup never had, and logged a mismatch on every load. The comment beside the script asserted the opposite - 'suppressHydrationWarning is not needed: this touches <html>'s attribute, not any element React rendered' - and the running app had been disproving it since #42 merged. Fix is <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning> plus the comment rewritten to say what is true. The alternative was checked first and is unavailable: rendering data-density server-side needs a server, and the packaged renderer is output: export built on a machine that has never met the user; dropping the script brings back the flash it exists to prevent. The flag works one level deep, so it covers <html>'s own attributes and nothing inside <head> or <body>. WHAT IT COST, honestly: the console and only the console. Production hydration does not warn and React patches no attribute either way, so compact kept working and nothing on screen was wrong - which is also why every gate here was blind to it. It is a dev-mode message, no test reads a console, and the three density proofs from the MAR-440/MAR-420 pass photograph a fresh window by clicking the real control, a window with no stored preference to disagree about. It is every load only for a user who has CHOSEN compact; with the default stored the script writes nothing. Two regression tests in tests/density.test.ts: the flag must be on the <html> app/layout.tsx renders, and it must appear on exactly ONE element in app/ - it turns off a real check, so spreading it is how a genuine mismatch elsewhere stops being reported. Both were confirmed red with the fix reverted and green with it back, which is MAR-465's rule applied to a unit test. Their first draft failed against prose - /<html\b[^>]*>/ matched a backticked <html> in a comment and the file that only DESCRIBES the flag was counted as carrying it - so the scans strip comments now; that is the same confusion between a comment and the thing it describes that caused the defect. Evidence: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm test 65 files / 1204 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed (1202 before, these two); pnpm state:check valid with the same 7 recorded drift warnings; and next dev with dash.density=compact stored giving a clean console on / and /runs/detail across fresh loads, the attribute still applied, --density-row-y still 4px and the toggle still flipping both attribute and storage. pnpm verify:shell was not run LOCALLY - Electron was running from the main checkout and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing it - but CI's Windows shell-smoke job ran it on the branch tip b26107b and it passed: 70 proofs, zero failures, plus the advisory 6l with all three live sources answering. 70 is unchanged from the MAR-440/MAR-420 pass and that is the right number: this change adds no installed proof, and a count that moved would mean it had touched the installed loop. Built AGAINST MASTER rather than on PR #52, which was open and unmerged behind a GitHub Actions outage at the time; the reconciliation is recorded below. THE RENDERER NAMES A KIND OF FILE AND NEVER A FILE. workspace.selectInput carries an agent, a task and a role, and no path in either direction. Main opens dialog.showOpenDialog, reads the declared limits out of the manifest itself, and hands the runner a path the page never saw and could not have chosen - the shape connection.connect established, and the sharper version of it: a credential the renderer could name is one page script already held, while a path the renderer could name is one nobody chose. tests/shell.test.ts refuses a payload carrying source_path, path, file or directory OUTRIGHT rather than dropping the field, exactly as the connect case refuses a credential field, and tests/inputs-render.test.tsx asserts no Windows drive letter, /Users/ or /home/ appears in the rendered markup. NOTHING CAN WIDEN WHAT THE AGENT DECLARED. role_id is checked against the manifest in main via declaredLimitsFor and a role the agent never declared is refused BEFORE A PICKER OPENS, so a person is not asked for a document that could not have been used. The limits travel from the manifest rather than from the payload: a renderer-supplied limit block could only be obeyed - letting a page widen the author's declaration - or ignored, which is a field on the wire that means nothing and a later reader would believe. CARDS, NEVER A TABLE. MAR-491 measured every table in DASH at 375px and found a 1425px scroller in a 341px viewport; a new surface starting as a table would be a new instance of a defect this project already paid to remove. The render test asserts no <table> element. SELECTED, COPIED AND REJECTED ARE PER FILE, NOT PER ROLE, and a rejection carries the runner's own sentence verbatim. runner/workspace.ts already answers with a plain sentence per refusal, and a second vocabulary in DASH would be the thing that stays wrong the day the runner's limits move. The copied state says the one fact nobody would guess and the whole workspace design rests on: DASH took its own copy, so changing or moving the original now changes nothing about what the agent reads. There is no remove control, because the runner has no route that takes an admitted input back out - deliberately, per runner/server.ts's own note on what the task routes do not offer - so a control would be one DASH cannot honour, and one that faked it by hiding the card would be worse because the file would still reach the agent. PLAIN LANGUAGE THROUGHOUT: the role's label comes from the manifest and describeInputRole has no branch that can fall back to the id, because a fallback is how a raw id appears on screen the day a manifest omits a label. Media types are mapped to words a person recognises and an unmapped one is dropped rather than printed - application/pdf is a technical identifier by lib/copy/identifiers.ts's own rule. A role that narrowed nothing says nothing rather than 'any file', which would promise a person that a 4 GiB video is welcome when the runner's own ceilings still apply. RUN NOW DISPATCHES THE TASK, AND A REFUSAL STOPS THE RUN. That failure branch is the interesting half: an agent started before its task is bound reads an empty workspace, and one started after a dispatch that failed produces an output derived from nothing the person gave it. Both look exactly like a successful run from outside, which is why neither may happen quietly. The run id is DASH's; runner/task-api.ts files whatever the agent writes against the run bound here, which is how proof 9 finds the output, and the agent's own telemetry run id may differ. That seam is MAR-434's and is unchanged - what is new is that a person can cause it from the page rather than from a script. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, PLAINLY. (1) NO SHIPPED EXAMPLE MANIFEST DECLARES task_inputs, so the panel is invisible in the product until one does. A test asserts that of all five examples rather than leaving it to be discovered, and it is the same shape as describeConnectionCondition's revoked sentence and resolveAvailability's honest default: vocabulary and surface built before a producer exists. (2) The task id lives in page state, because DASH holds no such row and the runner has no route to list an agent's open tasks. Leaving the page before pressing Run now loses the selection, and reopening a SECOND task on return would orphan the first one's files rather than reuse them, which is why the page does not try. (3) The installed-shell proof MAR-507 asks for - a person selecting a file and getting an output back, driving the shell's own command channel rather than the runner's routes - is NOT written. proof 9 covers the runner's half at PR #48; this adds no proof and would need electron/smoke.ts, which PR #51 owns. The opening sentence this replaces said PR OPEN and NOT MERGED, which was true when written and is corrected here on the 2026-08-07 reconciliation pass. Linear stays In Progress on purpose: merged is the ceiling this issue can reach on its own, because nothing about a host is proven and MAR-489 owns the attended half - the entry's own last paragraph says so and that paragraph is unchanged. PRIOR NOTE: branch 000henrik/mar-497-runner-standalone cut from master at 38f0ced. WHAT ACTUALLY RUNS ON THE VPS. ADR 0007 chose this repository's runner as the remote process and left one follow-up unowned: the runner is bundled into the Electron app as dist/electron/runner.mjs and started by the Electron binary with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, and a host has no Electron binary to start it with. ADR 0007 AMENDMENT 1 answers it - THE HOST SUPPLIES NODE, DASH DOES NOT SHIP A RUNTIME - and pnpm build:runner-standalone is the artifact: dist/runner-standalone/ holding start.mjs, runner.mjs, contracts/, a package.json and a README, started with one command, node start.mjs. runner/main.ts, runner/server.ts and runner/endpoint.ts are untouched. THE PREFLIGHT IS ITS OWN MODULE AND ITS OWN BUNDLE, and that is the structural half. runner/store.ts imports node:sqlite at the top level, so a check living in that module graph would run AFTER the import it exists to check - on the host it is written for, it would never execute. runner/host-runtime.ts checks the major version against a floor and then actually RESOLVES the module, because a version comparison alone would be this repository carrying a changelog fact it cannot verify on the machine it is refusing; runner/standalone.ts hands over with a dynamic import. An unsuitable host exits 78 (EX_CONFIG) with a sentence naming what it found; a runner that started and failed still exits 1, and a deploy verb can branch on the difference without parsing English. The floor is Node 24 as a SUPPORT claim rather than the earliest version that might work: node:sqlite appeared in 22.5 and spent its first releases behind --experimental-sqlite, and a floor admitting a release where the module needs a flag would make the documented start command wrong on a host that satisfies the floor. contracts/ IS IN THE ARTIFACT BECAUSE THE SEARCH WOULD OTHERWISE FIND THE REPOSITORY. lib/contracts.ts walks up from its own module location, so an artifact carrying no schemas at all works perfectly under this repository and fails on a host at the first manifest - not at build time and not at start time. tests/runner-standalone.test.ts copies the artifact to a temporary directory with nothing above it, strips DASH_CONTRACTS_DIR and ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE from the child environment, and asserts the runner's own contracts: line names the artifact's own directory. That is the only arrangement in which the difference is visible. THE DATA DIRECTORY IS CREATED AND HARDENED HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED. On Windows it sits under a user profile whose ACL already excludes other principals; a VPS home directory does not, and this one holds the channel credential, the database and any file a person handed to an agent. standalone.ts applies runner/channel-secret.ts's own hardenOwnerOnly and refuses to start if the permissions cannot be PROVEN - the same rule one machine over. Default ~/.orchestratedash/runner; DASH_RUNNER_DATA_DIR wins when set. ONE CORRECTION IT FORCED, AND IT WAS LOAD-BEARING. runner_build is what electron/runner-process.ts compares before adopting a runner, and the algorithm hashed path.relative output and raw file bytes - both platform-dependent, which nothing had noticed because only one machine ever computed it. A Linux-built artifact beside a Windows-built shell, from one commit, would have reported DIFFERENT identities, so 'the host is running the build this DASH shipped' would have been false in the only situation anybody asks it. scripts/runner-build-id.mjs is now the one implementation, folding path separators to / and CRLF to LF (this repository has no .gitattributes and core.autocrlf is on by default on Windows). Every input is TypeScript or JSON, so there is no binary to corrupt. scripts/build-shell.mjs loses its inline copy and gains an import - a small conflict with PR #51, which also touches that file. dash:node ALREADY MEANS THE RIGHT THING ON A HOST, which the issue listed as an open question and which the sentinel's name does not suggest. resolveSpawnCommand returns the SPAWNING process's own execPath plus ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1; on a host the spawning process is the standalone runner under the host's own Node, so it resolves to that Node and the variable is a flag plain Node has no opinion about. No host-specific branch is needed and the reason the sentinel exists carries over intact - a registration must not name a real interpreter path, on a version-stamped MSIX root or on a host. It matters immediately rather than eventually: the SAMPLE AGENT is registered with exactly this sentinel and is the first thing anybody would deploy. Proven by starting a real child under the standalone runner rather than by reading the resolver. NOT DECIDED HERE AND DELIBERATELY: restart-on-boot (the artifact ships no service unit; runner/README.md item 3 and ADR 0007 both keep it as its own decision) and retention on the host (item 4 still says nothing prunes anything). Enrollment - minting or exchanging the remote runner's credential - is MAR-484's, not this issue's; item 6 of runner/README.md is unchanged. EVIDENCE: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm state:check valid with the 8 recorded drift warnings; full vitest 73 files / 1384 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, including 19 new cases in tests/runner-standalone.test.ts; both build scripts report runner_build=96cef12082fe67afa3a6 from this tree, which is the identity claim above executed rather than asserted. Manual pass on Windows from PowerShell: the artifact copied outside the repository started under plain node, printed contracts: naming its own directory, listened on a named pipe, and stopped 202 through POST /shutdown. pnpm verify:shell IS RED ON THIS MACHINE AND NOT BECAUSE OF THIS BRANCH. 64 passed / 8 failed / 1 advisory, and the 8 are 6f, 6g, 6h, 9b, 9c, 9d, 9e and 9g - every one downstream of '[runner] request failed: database disk image is malformed'. The identical 8 fail on master's own tree in the same session, so this branch adds none. MAR-506's quarantine of %APPDATA%/orchestratedash/runner.sqlite HAS NOT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: the directory runner-sqlite-malformed-20260806 exists and is EMPTY, and a read-only DatabaseSync open of the live runner.sqlite still answers 'database disk image is malformed'. Nothing was worked around and nothing was moved; the gate cannot go green on this machine until that store is quarantined for real. NOTHING ABOUT A HOST IS PROVEN. What CI proves is the artifact starting under plain Node on a tree containing only itself, serving a task over its own socket, and stopping through the authenticated route. ssh, the deploy verbs and a real VPS are ADR 0004's permanently attended half and MAR-489 owns them.

Editing next.config.mjs made that server restart itself and the page hydrated in 268ms, same code, same machine, same port. WHY NOBODY NOTICED IT HAD GONE STALE: hot reload had never worked on this origin. Next blocks cross-origin access to its own dev resources for any host not in allowedDevOrigins and the default list omits the literal loopback address lib/shell/window.ts deliberately requires - it refuses localhost on purpose because a name resolves through DNS. Two individually correct decisions, and their intersection logged 'Blocked cross-origin request to Next.js dev resource /_next/webpack-hmr from 127.0.0.1' into .next/dev/logs/next-development.log where nobody reads. WHY NO GATE CAUGHT IT, which is the larger half: scripts/verify-shell.mjs forces DASH_SHELL_URL=dash-app://ui/ so the mandatory proof depends only on this repository and this machine (ADR 0004) - right, unchanged, and its consequence is that the gate has never once loaded the developer path. Proof 1 counts headings the server had already delivered; proof 2d calls window.dashData from the harness, which is not the page. Both are the shape MAR-473 named when 6j asserted only that A verdict existed. THE ASSERTION IS AN ABSENCE because a frozen shell is not missing content: since MAR-432 every page opens in a loading state and leaves it in an effect, so data-view-state=loading still present after the budget means no effect ever ran. lib/shell/first-paint.ts owns the rule; smoke proof 1f and pnpm shell:check evaluate the same probe so they cannot drift. pnpm shell also stops launching against a renderer it cannot vouch for (lib/shell/preflight.ts): nothing listening, another application on the port, an error status, or an export older than the source it is built from. It deliberately does not claim the page will work - no HTTP probe distinguishes a healthy page from a frozen one, and the comment says so where the next reader looks. Its child MAR-518 wired the repair to a button and is also merged; neither has been exercised installed against a genuinely damaged store, which is what would move either to proven. PRIOR NOTE: Branch 000henrik/mar-506-runner-store-damage, cut from master 38f0ced after confirming that commit is master's tip, so there is no reconciliation merge to read. THE FAULT: on 2026-08-06 a pnpm verify:shell run found runner.sqlite malformed, eight smoke checks failed on it and nothing else, and what a person saw was 'The runner answered 500.' That sentence names the transport. Everything they needed is elsewhere - DASH reached the runner, the runner is running, nothing of theirs is lost, and no agent will start until it is fixed. DETECTED TWICE, BECAUSE ONCE IS NOT ENOUGH. The issue asks whether the runner should detect SQLITE_CORRUPT at open rather than 500-ing per request; the honest answer is both, and the reported machine is the argument, because the store OPENED. journal_mode, synchronous, foreign_keys and the migration check all succeeded - a header page and a user_version live on pages that were intact - and only the queries against damaged leaves threw. So openRunnerStore runs PRAGMA quick_check, which walks pages rather than the header, and classifyStoreError runs again inside createRunnerServer's catch on whatever any route throws. quick_check rather than integrity_check: the extra work integrity_check does is cross-checking every index against its table, which is not what this is looking for, and a startup probe that made launching DASH visibly slower is a probe somebody eventually deletes. THE TEST THAT CARRIES IT builds that exact file - a real SQLite database with 400 real rows, header and schema page left alone, every later page overwritten with noise - and asserts the naive checks STILL PASS on it before asserting the probe does not. Take the quick_check out of openRunnerStore and that is the only test in the file that fails, which is the whole argument for the probe. A RUNNER WHOSE RECORDS ARE UNREADABLE SUPERVISES NOTHING, and that is a decision rather than a consequence: the supervisor does not need the database to spawn a child. It needs it for replay protection, idempotency and the approval record, which is every guarantee DASH renders about a command being carried out once and having been approved by somebody. An agent running against a store that cannot record is an agent whose guarantees DASH is still printing and no longer keeping, and that is worse than an agent that is not running, because the second one is visible. It still listens: /health reports store_damaged (a liveness fact carrying no path and no classification, so the unauthenticated route's rule survives), /shutdown stops it, /store/retire repairs it, and every other route answers one shape - 503 with reason store_damaged and a kind - rather than the 500 a thrown query used to produce. A runner that exited here would have left DASH with 'the runner did not start', which names nothing and offers no repair. THE REPAIR RENAMES AND NEVER DELETES. runner/store.ts records that the runner's database is the one place a user's free-text approval reason comes to rest, and a damaged database is frequently still readable by a recovery tool, so deleting it would destroy the only copy of a record DASH deliberately keeps nowhere else in order to fix a fault the user did not cause. The -wal and -shm siblings move under the database's NEW name rather than their own, so a recovery tool opening the set-aside file finds its log where SQLite looks for it. Retiring a healthy store is refused with 409 rather than performed. POST /store/retire sits above the damage guard and BELOW the authentication check, which is the interesting ordering: a runner that could be made to abandon its replay records by anybody who reached its socket would have a way to make an executed command executable again. storeDamage, database and workspace became functions on RunnerServerOptions for one reason - the answers change when a store is retired, and a server holding what it was constructed with would be a repair that repaired nothing until a relaunch. THE COPY: describeRunnerStoreDamage in lib/copy/recovery.ts keeps three kinds apart because they lead somewhere different - real damage; a file that was never a database, which is usually a sync client's conflict copy or a restore from the wrong place and where blaming the disk would send somebody after a hardware fault that is not there; and one DASH could not open, which is a permission or a lock, is not damage, and is NEVER offered a repair that throws the file away. Every branch says the two things a person actually needs and that separate this from describeStoreDamage: their own agents, runs and sign-ins are intact, and nothing is running. Tested plain-language, and tested to contain no '500', no 'answered', and no sqlite/disk-image vocabulary on any of its six branches. can_retire IS FALSE AT THE TRANSPORT TODAY, and that is the honest value rather than a placeholder. The runner CAN set a damaged store aside - POST /store/retire is built and tested end to end against a genuinely corrupt file - but nothing in DASH asks it to yet, because that wants a shell command in lib/shell/ipc.ts, a preload method, a main-process dispatch and a control on a surface, and four of those five files are owned by open PR #52. describeStoreDamage makes the same call for its unnamed case and says why: a next action the user cannot take is worse than one that admits DASH cannot fix this, because the first sends them looking for a button that is not on the screen. Flipping the flag is the last line of the follow-up that wires the control, and the copy is already written for it. ONE CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING: /health's body ok field now means 'and my store is readable', so smoke proof 4b goes red on a damaged store where eight scattered checks used to. That is the honest outcome and a better one - one early failure whose printed body says store_damaged, instead of eight later ones that each name the feature they were about. electron/smoke.ts is untouched (PR #51 owns it) and 4b's label now understates what it checks. EVIDENCE: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm state:check valid with the 8 recorded drift warnings; full vitest from PowerShell excluding the two stale .claude/worktrees directories, 73 files / 1378 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, of which 27 are the new tests/runner-store-damage.test.ts. pnpm verify:shell NOT run and recorded as not run: this machine's runner store is the damaged one the issue is about, so a shell smoke here would have been testing the fault rather than the fix, and the repair is not wired to a surface that could clear it. OVERLAP with the open PRs: none. lib/agent-dom/transport.ts, lib/copy/recovery.ts, runner/** and the tests are touched by no other open branch.

issues.note: MERGED to master in PR #63 (merge commit 96a70b8) on 2026-08-07; the sentence saying PR OPEN and NOT MERGED was written before that merge. PRIOR NOTE: MAR-506's own child, and the half PR #59 deliberately did not build: POST /store/retire existed and can_retire was hardcoded false because nothing in DASH asked for the repair yet. Branch 000henrik/mar-518-retire-store-surface cut from master at 354c93c. ALL FIVE FILES THE ISSUE NAMED: lib/shell/ipc.ts gains runner.retireStore in both COMMANDS and RUNNER_LIFECYCLE, naming no agent - a damaged store is a fact about the runner, not about any one agent it supervises, which is also why runnerLifecycle's new retireStore branch in electron/main.ts reaches POST /store/retire directly rather than an agent's own /lifecycle route. electron/preload.ts gains two bridge methods, not one: retireRunnerStore following connectConnection's shape as the issue asked, and runnerStatus beside it - undiscussed in the issue's own file list but load-bearing, because runner.status, runner.start, runner.stop and runner.remove were ALL wired end to end in the dispatcher and NEVER once exposed through dashShell, so there was no way for any page to learn a store was damaged in the first place. app/_data/source.ts gains checkRunnerStatus and retireRunnerStore, both following downloadOutput's refusal shape. THE STATUS BRANCH WAS ALSO WRONG, not just unreached: it called response.json() unconditionally, and fetch does not throw on a non-2xx status - only on a transport failure - so a damaged store's typed 503 parsed as {agents: undefined}, (body.agents ?? []).length was 0, and runner.status reported {ok: true, supervising: 0}: a healthy, idle runner, which is the opposite of true. Fixed by checking response.ok first and classifying the body with lib/agent-dom/transport.ts's own readStoreDamage, exported for this rather than reimplemented, so main.ts and the per-agent transport path cannot drift on what counts as damaged. RunnerStoreDamageNotice renders describeRunnerStoreDamage(kind, {can_retire: true}) as the three-part recovery plus a real button - the button the per-agent path can never have, because it has no surface to put one on. THE LAST LINE, DONE LAST: lib/agent-dom/transport.ts's can_retire flips from false to true, exactly as the issue's own comment said it would; that path's copy now reads as text what the home page's button lets somebody actually do. Relabelled 'the runner is listening and its store answers', assertion unchanged. NOT DONE: no automatic retirement anywhere, per the issue's own Do Not - the click is the consent, and nothing here retires a store without a person pressing the button that says so. MERGED to master, and in TWO parts from one branch: PR #54 (merge commit 9a150d7) and then PR #57 (merge commit 7d1eb03), both on 2026-08-06/07. The later one is recorded as the commit because it is the tip of what this issue put on master. The opening sentence this replaces said PR OPEN and NOT MERGED, corrected here on the 2026-08-07 reconciliation pass. Linear stays In Progress: merged is the ceiling, because nothing here has reached a host and MAR-489 owns the attended half - the entry's own last paragraph says so and is unchanged. The assumption below that #53 lands first HELD: MAR-497's PR #53 merged as b784df0 before this branch's first merge, so ADR 0007's amendment numbering is as written. PRIOR NOTE: branch 000henrik/mar-484-ssh-dialer-host-record cut from master at 38f0ced. Independent of MAR-497's branch; the only coupling is that both append to docs/adr/0007. THE EXCLUSION ADR 0007 CALLS STRUCTURAL IS STRUCTURAL NOW. lib/agent-dom/runner-channel.ts is the file the ADR's load-bearing paragraph was a finding about the absence of. What makes it impossible comes BEFORE any type: a broker-capable channel is built on ipcFetch, which dials a socketPath - there is no host in it, no name to resolve and no route to a network, and the URL it carries is the reserved .invalid TLD so a leak into a real fetch fails closed. The types are that fact made checkable in an editor. RunnerChannel<Route> takes a ROUTE rather than a URL, because ${origin}/broker/drain is a string types cannot see into; call is a PROPERTY with a function type and never a method, because TypeScript checks method parameters bivariantly even under strictFunctionTypes and the method spelling would have made the whole module decoration. TWO GUARDS, WATCHED FAILING, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME GUARD. Widening the remote channel's route set turns the call-site @ts-expect-error into TS2578; removing the capability brand alone turns NOTHING red, because parameter contravariance already excludes the assignment; removing both turns both assertions red. So the phantom unique-symbol brand earns its one cast by surviving somebody deciding the two route sets should be the same. A third guard scans lib/ and electron/ for the route strings IN CODE - comments are stripped, because electron/ssh-host.ts naming both routes to explain why it cannot carry them is the opposite of the thing being caught - which catches a hand-rolled fetch that bypassed the channel entirely. That is MAR-465's rule applied to a type: a gate nobody has seen fail is not known to work. electron/broker-host.ts is the one production change and it is what makes the property load-bearing rather than decorative: startBroker now builds a LocalRunnerChannel and names routes instead of concatenating them onto an origin. electron/agent-adapters.ts is UNTOUCHED, deliberately - generalising its drains is MAR-488's work, and it is now safe to do, which was the entire point. lib/agent-dom/transport.ts, runner/server.ts and runner/endpoint.ts are untouched as ADR 0007 said they would be. THE DIALER IS ipcFetch's MOVE A SECOND TIME. lib/agent-dom/ssh-fetch.ts is a fetch-shaped function over a child process's stdio, and it is deliberately NOT an HTTP parser: node:http's client takes a createConnection that may return any duplex stream, so the request line, header encoding, chunked transfer and every edge case around them are Node's - byte for byte the code that serves the local runner. What this module contributes is a duplex over a child's two pipes plus the no-op socket methods the HTTP client calls (setKeepAlive, setNoDelay, setTimeout, ref, unref); setTimeout is a no-op ON PURPOSE, because the deadline that governs this transport is transport.ts's AbortSignal and a second timer would give a remote channel a different timeout story from a local one. ssh is spawned per request rather than pooled: a pool would be faster and would make the failure model much worse. THE DEPLOY PLANE'S VERSION OF 'NEVER WHAT TO RUN'. ssh takes its options as argv and argv has no quoting layer to get wrong, so an address of -oProxyCommand=... is not an address, it is a flag. lib/hosts.ts refuses any component reaching argv that begins with '-' as its OWN named problem rather than folded into malformed, and allowlists the rest. sshArgv's absences matter as much as its presences: BatchMode=yes because a prompt with no terminal is a hang in the poll loop; StrictHostKeyChecking=yes against DASH's OWN known_hosts and never the user's, because an entry DASH added to ~/.ssh would outlive DASH and change how the person's own ssh behaves; not accept-new, which would silently trust a new key the first time an address changed; IdentitiesOnly=yes and IdentityAgent=none so exactly one key is offered and the ssh-agent ADR 0007 declined cannot come back through a config file; and NO -L, -R or -D, because option 2 was rejected for MAR-430's reason and the way that stays true is that the flag is never passed. The verb set is closed with exactly one member, connect - ADR 0007 put the rest with the deploy bridge and writing them now would be vocabulary for an implementation that does not exist. CUSTODY, STATED AS AN ABSENCE. The key is minted by the machine's own ssh-keygen, protected with runner/channel-secret.ts's hardenOwnerOnly - the same function, not a second implementation, which is what keeps the Swedish-Administrator bug from coming back in a new file - and PROVEN AGAIN immediately before every use. No passphrase, because a passphrase on a key DASH uses unattended would have to be stored where DASH can read it: a second credential protecting the first one, kept beside it. And electron/ssh-host.ts HAS NO FUNCTION THAT RETURNS A PRIVATE KEY. It can create one, protect one, prove one and name the path ssh should read. DASH cannot leak what it never reads, and a test asserts it over the module's own exports rather than trusting a header - which is where somebody would add a reader, because the deploy plane will one day want to 'just check' the key. Only the public half is returned, because that is the one thing that should travel. EVIDENCE: pnpm typecheck clean; full vitest 75 files / 1400 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, 53 of them new across tests/broker-channel-exclusion.test.ts (10), tests/ssh-fetch.test.ts (11) and tests/host-record.test.ts (32). The compile-time exclusion was watched failing in all three directions recorded above. One test-only correction: the six cases that spawn ssh-keygen, whoami and icacls carry a stated 60s budget - alone they take under a second, and under full-suite load on Windows they exceeded vitest's 5s default and went red on a timeout rather than on a defect, which is MAR-472's lesson with the assertions unchanged. INSTALLED-SHELL EVIDENCE FOR THE ONE PRODUCTION CHANGE: pnpm verify:shell on this branch is 64 passed / 8 failed, and PROOF 8 (8a-8f) IS AMONG THE PASSES - that is the real Electron shell driving the refactored broker loop end to end, 200 requests sent by the agent, 64 adjudicated, 136 dropped, drained through /broker/drain and answered through /broker/responses over the typed channel. The 8 failures are 6f, 6g, 6h, 9b, 9c, 9d, 9e and 9g, byte-identical to the set that fails on master's own tree in the same session and every one downstream of '[runner] request failed: database disk image is malformed'. MAR-506's quarantine of %APPDATA%/orchestratedash/runner.sqlite still has not happened - the directory runner-sqlite-malformed-20260806 exists and is EMPTY. Nothing was worked around. NOTHING HERE HAS REACHED A HOST. No ssh runs in any test, no host record is persisted, and no surface connects one - that is MAR-498. What is proven is the dialer, the record's refusals, the command's shape and the key's custody. ADR 0004 keeps the rest attended and dated, permanently, and MAR-489 owns it.

issues.note: TWO HALVES, LIKE MAR-434. The DESIGN half merged in PR #55 (merge commit d1bed30) on 2026-08-06 and its entry recorded, deliberately, that the issue's own merged bar — every state of the flow rendered and screenshotted at the three widths electron/capture.ts covers — was NOT met. The SURFACE half MERGED to master in PR #75 (merge commit ad2b1bd) on 2026-08-07, verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` before this lifecycle moved, and the commit field moves from the design half's d1bed30 to it. The sentence that stood here said PR OPEN and NOT MERGED and moved the lifecycle back to planned for the half then in flight; both were right when written and both are corrected now. Branch 000henrik/mar-498-connect-a-host, cut from 000henrik/mar-533-connections-capability-cards. Four steps, drawn in MAR-528's Bit-Command system: a numbered rail with connectors, provider cards, inset fields and a receipt. THE INVERSION IS THE WHOLE DESIGN AND IT IS RENDERED AS A SENTENCE. The concept screen for this flow has an SSH_PRIVATE_KEY textarea with a BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY placeholder and a save-key-to-vault checkbox. DASH draws no such field: MAR-484 made key custody structural rather than a policy — electron/ssh-host.ts has NO FUNCTION THAT RETURNS A PRIVATE KEY and a test asserts that over the module's exports rather than trusting a comment, because that is where somebody would add a reader when the deploy plane one day wants to just check it. So step 3 shows the PUBLIC half and where to put it, AND SAYS THE REFUSAL OUT LOUD: somebody who has connected a server before expects to be asked, every other tool asks, and a flow that quietly does not ask reads as one that forgot rather than as one that decided. tests/host-wizard-render.test.tsx checks the markup rather than the copy for this, because the failure mode is somebody adding an input and not somebody removing a sentence. THE PROVIDER CARDS RECOMMEND NOTHING, RANK NOTHING AND LINK NOWHERE — MAR-485 owns provider recommendations and affiliate links and is an explicit non-goal here. They answer the one question a novice cannot get from the outside, which is the account name, and Something else is a first-class choice that says DASH does not know rather than guessing. THE DEPLOY RECEIPT RENDERS SOMEWHERE AT LAST: lib/deploy/bundle.ts has built it since MAR-487 and nothing showed it. ADR 0007 requires the while-closed sentence BEFORE THE FIRST DEPLOY, and the moment a server becomes reachable is the last point at which that is still true, so it is on step 4. describeDeployArrangement is the base and the agent-named describeDeployReceipt is the wrapper rather than the other way round: two copies of a disclosure are two copies that can be softened independently, and the one that would get softened is the one somebody reads while deciding. THE DEFECT THIS BRANCH INTRODUCED AND THE GUARD THAT MISSED IT, recorded because it is the more useful half. Importing that receipt put node:crypto in the browser bundle and the packaged renderer STOPPED HYDRATING ALTOGETHER — every page drew its background colour and nothing else, no chrome, no agents, no error on screen, and it was found by looking at the screenshots rather than by any gate. tests/client-bundle.test.ts exists for exactly this and PASSED, because its Node-only list was five strings somebody typed and lib/deploy/bundle was not among them. The list is now COMPUTED: lib/ is walked, every module importing a node: builtin is marked, and the mark propagates up the import graph to a fixed point, so a module written tomorrow that reads from disk is on the list the moment it exists. The five original names are kept as a floor, because a walk that broke and returned an empty set would pass that file forever, which is the failure being fixed arriving through a different door. Two capture-harness fixes, both found by running it: a splash that closes during a capturePage retry no longer ends a run holding 47 unwritten images, and a window that closes between its photograph and its measurement now loses the caption rather than the frame. NOT WIRED, AND THE PAGE SAYS SO WHERE THE EFFECT WOULD HAVE HAPPENED: there is no host command family, so nothing here mints a key, writes a record or runs a probe. That is MAR-536. The six unreachable states the surface therefore cannot reach are covered by tests/host-wizard-render.test.tsx instead, which is the more durable half of the issue's own bar — a screenshot proves a state was drawn once on one machine. Evidence: pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm brand:check green, 98 test files / 1810 passed / 8 skipped from PowerShell, 30 of them new. 55 images in qa-screenshots-mar-498, page_overflows: false and density_toggle.fully_visible: true at every width with SIX nav links, which is MAR-491's wrapping decision surviving a sixth destination. MERGED to master in PR #61 (merge commit 6020a9e) on 2026-08-07; the sentence below saying PR OPEN and NOT MERGED, so no commit is claimed here yet, was written before that merge. Linear moves Todo -> In Progress, meaning merged-and-not-proven. AND IT IS NOW PARTLY PROVEN BY SOMETHING THIS PACKET CAN CITE: the 2026-08-07 attended run passed G2 for the first time ever - a real consent, a real token exchange carrying this secret, and a refresh token in the DPAPI vault (G2/G3) - which is the exact failure MAR-468's 2026-08-06 run produced and this issue was filed for. It is not promoted to proven because that run FAILED at G9 and the runbook's promotion rule is that a run failing any check promotes nothing. See MAR-523, which is the single thing between that run and a green one. PRIOR NOTE: URGENT, and it is the finding MAR-468's attended proof exists to produce. Found 2026-08-06 by the first execution of that proof. lib/oauth/flow.ts sends NO client_secret - not in exchangeAuthorizationCode, not in refreshAccessToken - and OAuthProvider in lib/oauth/providers.ts declares no field that could carry one. Google, asked directly with exactly the parameters DASH sends and a deliberately invalid code: 'HTTP 400 {error: invalid_request, error_description: client_secret is missing.}'. It rejects the request before looking at the code at all. So DASH's Google OAuth HAS NEVER WORKED against real Google and could not have; revokeGrant is unaffected because Google's revocation endpoint takes only the token. WHY EVERY GATE IS BLIND TO IT: proof 7 drives OAuth against the loopback provider whose token_endpoint is a path on an origin the harness binds for itself, a fixture which naturally never asks for a client secret. The whole OAuth path is exercised end to end against a server that cannot reject it for the one reason the real one does. That is precisely the substitution ADR 0002 amendment 1 described and MAR-468 was filed to close. WHAT IT FALSIFIES: ADR 0002 amendment 3's point 2, in writing - that a green attended run would establish PKCE, the ephemeral loopback redirect, access_type=offline and prompt=consent really do yield a refresh token. They do not. The amendment's guess that G8b, the projection over a real MIME tree, was 'the single most likely thing here to have been wrong' was also wrong: the run never reached G8b. MAR-446's acceptance criteria about real Google sign-in were met against a test server and should be re-read. THE DECISION IT NEEDED, which is why it was not a one-line fix: where the secret comes from. (1) compiled in beside the client id; (2) supplied locally and not committed, via an environment variable; (3) bring-your-own client (MAR-471), the real product answer. THIS SESSION PICKED OPTION 2 and built it, on branch 000henrik/mar-508-google-oauth-client-secret cut from master at 354c93c. PR OPEN and NOT MERGED; merge left to Henrik per merge:human-gated, so no commit is claimed here yet. `DASH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, read fresh on every call by a new `googleClientSecret()` in lib/oauth/providers.ts rather than once at import - the same choice `loopbackProofOrigin()` already made, for the same reason: a module-load-time read is invisible to a test that sets the variable per case. `OAuthProvider` gained an optional `client_secret`; `GOOGLE` (a const) became `googleProvider()` (a function) so the env read happens per call; the loopback proof provider deliberately declares none, so proof 7 sends no client_secret exactly as before - NOT WEAKENED. `exchangeAuthorizationCode` and `refreshAccessToken` in lib/oauth/flow.ts both send `client_secret` in the POST body when the provider declares one and omit the key entirely - not an empty string, not the literal 'undefined' - when it does not. THE TEST THE ISSUE ASKED FOR: tests/oauth-flow.test.ts's new 'the client secret (MAR-508)' block builds a provider literal with client_secret set and a fetch that captures the outgoing form body, asserting client_secret reaches the wire on both the code exchange and a refresh - the loopback fixture cannot mask this because the assertion never touches the fixture's response, only the request DASH sent. A neighbouring case pins that a provider declaring none sends none. Options 1 and 3 are still undecided; this session decided nothing about either. FOLDED IN, the issue's own 'also worth revisiting': lib/copy/recovery.ts's describeAuthorizationFailure used to give provider_error and provider_refused identical copy - 'refused the sign-in... an account managed by a workplace or school'. provider_refused is what postForm throws for any token-endpoint rejection other than invalid_grant, and per RFC 6749 Section 5.2 every one of those (invalid_request, invalid_client, unauthorized_client, unsupported_grant_type) is the provider validating DASH's own request, not the account - a missing client_secret produced exactly this code. It now reads 'DASH's Google sign-in request was rejected... a fault in how DASH asked', actor 'dash'. provider_error (lib/oauth/loopback.ts's reading of the authorization redirect itself carrying an error= the provider put there) keeps the original account-level wording, since that is a real signal about the account. tests/oauth-flow.test.ts pins both the actor and that the two sentences no longer match. docs/real-google-proof-runbook.md documents DASH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET as new step 1a and corrects its own status paragraph: the fix has landed but the attended run has not been repeated. EVIDENCE: pnpm typecheck clean; full vitest from PowerShell (Git Bash's whoami fakes channel-secret failures), 85 test files / 1611 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, 4 of them new. pnpm verify:shell NOT run this session - a runner from an earlier, unrelated failed google-proof attempt (dist/google-proof/runner.mjs) was found still alive and orphaned on this machine, and starting the shell smoke alongside it risked exactly the kind of interference AGENTS.md's process-safety rule exists to avoid; it was left alone rather than force-killed. NOT PROVEN: nobody has stood at a real Google consent screen with this fix in place. That is the next attended MAR-468 run, and it needs DASH_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET set in the operator's shell first.

Two defects in MAR-468's attended harness, found 2026-08-06 by attempting to run it, fixed on branch 000henrik/prove-google-launcher-einval at 7da5c54 and 800e0f6, MERGED to master in PR #56 (merge commit 99fa58b) on 2026-08-07. This entry's own predecessor called the branch 'NOT merged - no PR opened yet'; that sentence is corrected here, the same way MAR-473, MAR-467, MAR-441, MAR-474, MAR-469 and MAR-476 each corrected their own predecessor's pre-merge sentence. Neither defect is in product code: lib/, electron/, runner/ are untouched and scripts/google-proof/'s checks are unchanged. (1) IT NEVER LAUNCHED ELECTRON. scripts/prove-google.mjs spawned node_modules/.bin/electron.cmd, and since the fix for CVE-2024-27980 Node refuses to spawn a .cmd without shell:true - spawnSync returns EINVAL having started nothing. result.error was never inspected, so process.exit(result.status ?? 1) printed nothing at all: the operator saw two banner lines and their shell prompt back, which reads exactly like a proof that ran and found nothing to say. issues.note: PR OPEN and NOT MERGED, branch 000henrik/mar-537-runner-standalone-flake cut from master at ad2b1bd after confirming that commit is master's tip, so there is no reconciliation merge to read. A FLAKY BLOCKING GATE, AND THE CAUSE IS AN ORDERING BUG RATHER THAN SLOWNESS. tests/runner-standalone.test.ts asserts on the runner's first four startup lines and reached them by polling for runner.json. That file is a STRICTLY EARLIER EVENT than the lines: runner/main.ts writes it at line 349, immediately after listenOnEndpoint resolves, and prints `listening on`, `store:` and `contracts:` at lines 367-372 afterwards. So the wait ended, by construction, at a moment when the child might not have printed any of them — and under load, where it is the PARENT's own stdout `data` callbacks that run late, it regularly had not. The 100ms poll interval is why this looked rare: the three console.warn calls land microseconds after the write, so only a parent descheduled inside that window loses them. THE OBSERVED SIGNATURE WAS THEREFORE A LIE ABOUT ITS OWN SUBJECT: `expected '[runner] standalone start: node=24.18…' to contain '[runner] listening on'` is a truncated string blaming the built artifact for a race in the harness observing it, on a commit (PR #75) that changed one block comment in electron/capture.ts. THE FIX IS THE ISSUE'S OWN FIRST PREFERENCE, and it SUBSUMES the old wait rather than sitting beside it: waitForLine reads the child's output until `[runner] contracts: <artifact>/contracts` appears, and because runner.json is written before that line is printed, the file is present whenever the line has arrived. issues.note: MERGED 2026-08-09 via PR #93 (bc28035). Originally: PR #93 (https://github.com/orchestratemcp/orchestratedash/pull/93), branch 000henrik/mar-575-smoke-log, cut from origin/master at bc62e61 in its own worktree (../dash-mar575). No commit is claimed; merging is left to Henrik. THE ISSUE'S OWN THEORIZED MECHANISM IS NOT WHAT WAS HAPPENING, and this was confirmed against real CI rather than assumed. MAR-575 asked to check the alternative (the detached runner inheriting stdout) before fixing on the app.exit-races-drain theory; both were checked. The runner does not inherit this process's stdout -- electron/runner-process.ts already redirects it to runner.log on disk, specifically to avoid an EPIPE once the parent exits -- so that alternative is ruled out directly from the source. The drain theory was tested more rigorously: a deliberately-failing late proof (9h) was pushed with NO fix, producing a real 'before' run (31278451508) that truncated at 6a via `gh run view --log`, exactly as the issue describes. But the RAW stored log (`gh api repos/.../actions/jobs/<id>/logs`) was COMPLETE in that same run -- every proof through 9h and the [smoke] FAILED summary were all present. Nothing was lost at the source. The stdout/stderr-drain fix was then applied and CI re-run (31279210553): `gh run view --log` STILL truncated at the identical point, no change, while the raw log was (again) already complete without the fix. THE REAL CAUSE: proof 6b was logging one ~150KB single JSON line -- check() serialized the shipped sample agent's entire file bundle (manifest + full source) inline via `check("6b. ...", created.ok, created)`. Line-oriented readers commonly cap what they buffer for a single line; Go's bufio.Scanner, which gh's CLI is built on, defaults to 64KB and stops silently past it. That explains 'always stops at the same proof, in both a failing and a green run' as a deterministic function of line length rather than a race dependent on timing, and matches what a human reading the job in GitHub's own log viewer plausibly saw. FIX, TWO PARTS. check() now caps a serialized detail at 8,000 characters with a truncation marker, so no future proof's detail object can reintroduce this class of defect by accident -- ADR 0004's 'by construction rather than by convention' applied to the harness's own output rather than to a release gate. And 6b logs a summary (agent id, directory, per-file byte counts) instead of file contents, which is more useful to a reader as well as smaller. THE DRAIN FIX STAYS, as defense in depth rather than as the confirmed fix: app.exit racing an async pipe write is still a real, separate risk that could matter under different conditions (a genuinely slow CI log consumer, a genuinely large legitimate backlog), even though it was not what produced this issue's symptom. flushOutputThenExit writes a trailing empty chunk to stdout then stderr and exits from the second callback, with a 15s unref'd fallback timer bounding a pipe that never drains at all. EVIDENCE, all via CI runs on this PR using the exact tool (`gh run view --log`) that exhibited the original symptom: before (31278451508) truncates at 6a; intermediate (31279628021, size-cap fix in, demo failure still present) shows 9h's own line and the FAILED summary reaching the log for the first time; after (31279893453, demo failure removed) is green end to end with `[smoke] all proofs passed` printed. issues.note:
MERGED 2026-08-09 via PR #95 (dd96ba2). Originally: branch 000henrik/mar-576-agent-output-first, cut from origin/master at bc62e61 in its own worktree (../dash-mar576). No commit is claimed; merging is left to Henrik per this project's own record that merging from a Claude Code session is unreliable.

THE DIAGNOSIS WAS RUN ON HENRIK'S REAL STORE FIRST, AND IT REFUTED HALF THE PREDICTION. A VACUUM INTO snapshot of %APPDATA%/orchestratedash/dash.sqlite (read-only; the live file was never opened read-write) confirmed MAR-548's handoff on the manifest: ai-news-scout's stored document -- folder and row byte-identical, generated_by 'create-dash-agent 43.2.0', generated_at 2026-08-05T15:24:29Z -- has agent_dom keys dom_version, runtime, trigger, locations, connections, permissions, control, memory AND NO panel. Reconciliation is clean, no damage, no drift.

BUT THE SECOND HALF OF THE PREDICTION WAS WRONG, AND THIS IS THE FINDING THE ISSUE TURNED ON. The digest artifacts were all there -- 33 of them, kind 'digest', the newest carrying 9 items and 3 sources_fetched -- and the news WAS on the page the whole time. workspaceView resolves outputs from latestArtifactForAgent, resolveArtifactAvailability defaults to 'available' when no workspace row exists, canPreview passes, and OutputsPanel renders the digest through DigestBody. Nothing was missing and nothing was broken.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG WAS THE ORDER. Reproduced in the PACKAGED renderer against a scratch store seeded with Henrik's own manifest, digest and events: the first headline began at y=1166px on a 375px viewport that is 812px tall, and y=664 at 1280. Above it sat the files panel, Run now, a permission disclaimer, and -- inside the output card itself -- a four-row provenance receipt reading Made by / The agent's own time / Reached DASH / Size stored. That is 'only some text about that it ran' exactly. The agent's own output was the fifth thing on its own page, and inside its own card it came last.

THAT ALSO MEANS THE OBVIOUS FIX WOULD HAVE MADE IT WORSE. AgentPanel renders BELOW the Outputs area, so restoring the manifest alone would have put the declared digest surface even further down the page.

WHAT SHIPPED, AGAINST THE ISSUE'S THREE BARS.

(1) THE OUTPUT LEADS THE PAGE. OutputsArea moves directly under the identity header; inputs, Run now and the permission receipt drop below it. Inside the card, the body renders before the receipt and the receipt folds behind a 'How DASH got this' disclosure while the output is available -- inline when it is not, which is MAR-434's own argument for the receipt surviving preserved as a branch rather than deleted. news_top_px went 1166 -> 875 at 375 and 664 -> 487 at 1280.

ONLY DASH'S OWN SURFACES MOVED. The author's panel stays below them, so MAR-548's attribution argument -- that a `note` must not sit where a person reads DASH's own voice -- is untouched. Henrik chose that scope over promoting the panel too.

ONE DEFECT, TWO RENDERERS, AND ONLY THE PHOTOGRAPH HAD BOTH IN FRAME. app/_components/panel.tsx draws its OWN artifact card, so fixing the Outputs area fixed nothing inside the author's region. The packaged-renderer screenshot taken after pressing the new button showed the receipt still above the headlines in the box whose entire purpose is 'what did the scout find?'. Fixed there too, and pinned by a test.

(2) THE HONESTY SENTENCE. lib/sample-refresh.ts's describeManifestGap fires on exactly two conditions: the stored document carries DASH's own create-dash-agent provenance AND declares no panel. Narrow on purpose -- most agents declare no panel and for them the absence is the author's choice, so only a document DASH ITSELF WROTE can be behind DASH's own template. A malformed panel is deliberately excluded: resolvePanel already reports it as unreadable, and telling that person their agent is also old would be the wrong second diagnosis of one fault. The notice is DASH's voice about DASH's gap, so it renders outside the attributed region, not as a fourth PanelView case.

THE FIRST DRAFT OF THAT NOTICE WAS ITSELF THE DEFECT. Headline + five-line explanation + next action + button + four-line reassurance rendered 400px tall at 375px and put the news at 1156px -- within 10px of where the bug had it. A notice that explains why you cannot see something, by covering it, has fixed nothing. It is one sentence now (which is what the issue asked for), two-column above 28rem, and the 'nothing has been lost' reassurance was cut because with the output directly underneath it describes what the reader can already see. next_action survives as the way forward for the reader with NO button -- a browser tab, or a shell too old to have the command -- and renders only then.

(3) THE ONE-CLICK RE-IMPORT. New audited command sample.refresh, its own fifth family (SAMPLE_ACTIONS) rather than agent.* -- reserved for the contract's seven verbs -- or runner.*, since no process is started, stopped or asked anything. Payload is one agent id: page script can ask DASH to regenerate an agent FROM DASH'S OWN TEMPLATE and has no way to hand DASH a document to store. mutates true, irreversible false. THE OWNERSHIP GATE LIVES IN electron/main.ts BESIDE THE WRITE, not at the ipc seam, so no future caller can route around it; it reads the FOLDER first (ADR 0008 authority) and refuses anything create-dash-agent did not generate. It goes through the ordinary importManifest door, which writes folder-then-row, revalidates, clears the startup folder issue, and -- via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE omitting avatar -- is why the button's caption can promise the character survives. Identity (name, display_name, goal) comes from the stored document; capability comes from the template. Regenerating rather than patching in the missing panel means a scaffolded agent is never more than one press behind DASH itself. The agent's own project folder is never touched.

THE COMPILE-TIME ROUTING ASSERTION IN lib/shell/ipc.ts CAUGHT THE UNROUTED COMMAND ON THE FIRST TYPECHECK, which is what it was written for.

A TEST I WROTE WAS FALSE ABOUT THE SHIPPED PRODUCT, AND IS WORTH RECORDING. Having folded the Outputs receipt behind a <details>, folding the panel's was the obvious next step -- and neither smoke 6o nor tests/panel-render.test.tsx counts a <summary> as a control, so it would have passed everything while weakening ADR 0008's 'no toggle' claim. Adding <details> to the control list turned that red, and the reason was not my change: DigestBody has drawn 'Where this came from' inside the region since MAR-434, arriving from the ARTIFACT the same way a digest item's link does. So the assertion was wrong, not the code. The panel's receipt is simply moved below the body; the control list is unchanged and now carries the reason.

EVIDENCE. pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm brand:check green; pnpm state:check valid with the same 19 pre-existing merged/In-Progress drift warnings, none from this branch; full vitest from PowerShell 107 files / 2176 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed, 21 of them new. pnpm verify:shell RUN LOCALLY AND ALL PROOFS PASSED on this Windows machine -- including new proof 6p ({news_before_receipt:true, heading_before_receipt:true, has_receipt:true}), with 6n and 6o still green (controls_inside 0, raw_instants 0), which is what says the panel change did not cost ADR 0008 its strongest claim. 6p measures DOCUMENT ORDER via compareDocumentPosition rather than pixels: a height comparison would pass or fail on CI's window size, and document order is what a screen reader and a keyboard follow.

BOTH LOAD-BEARING TESTS WERE DEMONSTRATED FAILING FIRST. Dropping the provenance gate turns 'says nothing about a third-party agent that declares no panel' red and nothing else. Putting the receipt back above the body turns the two ordering assertions red and nothing else.

SCREENSHOTS: qa-screenshots-mar576/, packaged renderer (build:renderer then build:shell), 375 and 1280, light and dark, plus one taken AFTER pressing Update this agent showing panel_present true, heading 'What the scout found', the notice gone and news_top_px 410. Taken by a throwaway Electron probe that skipped smoke-identity -- own app name, own user-data dir, own single-instance lock -- so it ran beside the live DASH and never opened Henrik's records. Deleted rather than committed, per MAR-548's precedent.

NON-GOALS HELD: no schema edit (contracts/ belongs to MAR-569), no new panel section type.
