issues.note: MERGED 2026-08-09 via PR #94 (d7fc1e0). Originally: branch 000henrik/mar-572-host-enrollment, cut from origin/master at bc62e61 in its own worktree (../dash-mar572), beside a parallel MAR-574 session that owns app/hosts/page.tsx. No commit is claimed; merging is left to Henrik, per this project's record that merging from a Claude Code session is unreliable. WHAT THIS IS: the first-pin enrollment step ADR 0007 left as future work, plus the refusal split the 2026-08-08 attended run proved was needed. Written with MAR-573 on one branch because they are one journey - the enrollment wall is what a person hits first, and clearing it is what makes the bootstrap wall reachable at all. THE ENROLLMENT STEP: host.probe on a record whose host_fingerprint is null no longer dials. It runs ssh-keyscan over DASH's own dialer, computes the SHA256 fingerprint FROM THE BYTES (not by scraping ssh-keygen -l, so the string a person compares is pinned in CI against a vector OpenSSH produced), and returns host_key_not_trusted carrying fingerprint, key type and how many keys the server offered. host.trust is a new audited command that carries the fingerprint the person was SHOWN back to main; main asks the server again and refuses if the two disagree, which closes the window between showing a code and somebody clicking yes. Refusing writes nothing - that is structural, not a code path: nothing happens unless host.trust is called. THE HONESTY IS THE POINT. Trust on first use proves nothing; a fingerprint fetched over the connection it describes is self-consistent by construction. So the copy says 'DASH cannot check this for you - anything answering at this address could say the same thing, so this is the one part only you can confirm.' A screen with a fingerprint and a Confirm button and no such sentence teaches people that clicking yes IS a verification. A test asserts that sentence and that the state is never worded as an error. THERE IS NO RE-PIN, and it is enforced in three places that must all agree: pinHostKey has no argument that overwrites a line, pinHostFingerprint updates only WHERE host_fingerprint IS NULL, and trustHostKey returns the identity-changed alarm rather than a success when a record is already pinned. Re-adding a genuinely rebuilt server means forgetting it first, which removes DASH's key and its known_hosts line together (forgetHostKeyPin is new and is only reachable from host.forget). ADR 0007's fail-closed requirement therefore survives the new affordance, which is the thing an enrollment feature most easily breaks. THE REFUSAL SPLIT: HostReachProblem goes from six to nine - no_answer_at_address, host_key_not_trusted and helper_not_installed are new, each with its own next action, and the existing distinctness test covers them because it iterates HOST_REACH_PROBLEMS. classifyHostFailure is the new pure function that reads ssh's stderr and returns one of the nine or null. IT PARSES STDERR, WHICH openSshChannel PREVIOUSLY REFUSED TO DO, and the reason the refusal is now kept differently is recorded in ADR 0009: the old rule was kept by not looking, and the attended run priced that - three completely different failures arrived as one sentence and sent the operator to check a key on a server that had never been asked for one. The rule is now kept by the RETURN TYPE: the classifier can only return a member of a closed union, there is no branch that puts ssh's text into its result, and a reviewer checks that by reading the signature rather than auditing call sites. Its stderr cases are strings captured from real OpenSSH builds. null is a real return value and stays generic rather than guessing - a shrug sends nobody anywhere, a wrong classification sends them somewhere specific. RESUMABILITY AND KEY CHURN, the run's third finding: the wizard reset to step 1 on every failure and minted a FRESH KEY each pass, orphaning the previous key in DASH's store and leaving a stale line on the host. Fixed at the point where a key would be minted rather than in the wizard: host.create now calls findHostByConnection (address + port + username, deliberately not the label) and, when a record exists, reads the public half back with the new readHostPublicKey instead of minting. So there is no churn EVEN IF the page still resets - which matters because app/hosts/page.tsx belongs to MAR-574 and this session did not touch it. ONE CUSTODY GUARD WAS DELIBERATELY STRENGTHENED RATHER THAN DODGED. tests/host-record.test.ts sweeps electron/ssh-host.ts's exports for /^(read|export|get|load|reveal)/i + /key/i and expected none; readHostPublicKey trips it. Renaming it to evade the pattern was available and was declined - the guard's whole value is that a reader function is where the mistake lands. Instead the exemption is by exact name in a one-element list, AND the test now runs every exempted reader against a real minted pair and asserts it returns the same string minting returned, starts with ssh-ed25519, and contains nothing of the private half sitting next to it. That is strictly stronger than what it replaces, which checked no behaviour at all. WHAT MAR-574 MUST WIRE, EXACTLY: on a probe failure whose data.problem is host_key_not_trusted, read data.fingerprint / data.key_type / data.offered_count and render describeConnectState({ step: 'confirm_host_key', label, fingerprint, key_type, offered_count }); a Confirm button calls submitHostCommand('trust', { host_id, fingerprint }) with the SAME fingerprint that was displayed; on ok, re-probe. A Back button from the check step must NOT call forget - that is what mints a new key. host.create's result now also carries authorized_keys_line (the public half with restrict,command= in front, which is what should be shown for a hand install) and resumed (true when it attached to an existing server). EVIDENCE: pnpm typecheck clean; full vitest from PowerShell 108 files / 2177 passed / 10 skipped, with tests/host-key.test.ts new (fingerprint vectors from OpenSSH, blob-claims-its-own-type refusal, known_hosts port form including IPv6) and new cases in host-connect (the classifier, including that a changed key is never softened into an unconfirmed one), store (find-by-connection, pin-once) and host-record (the custody guard above). One unrelated file, tests/store-damage.test.ts, failed once under full parallel load and passed alone - the known flakiness on this machine. NOT RUN: any real host. This is fixture and string evidence only; the enrollment step has never met an sshd it did not already know, which is exactly the gap the next attended run closes. CI IS GREEN at aa56ad5 on PR #94 — verify SUCCESS (1m03s) and shell-smoke SUCCESS (1m35s), https://github.com/orchestratemcp/orchestratedash/actions/runs/31278697971. That matters twice here. THE CIRCLE, AND HOW IT IS BROKEN: ADR 0007 says the helper travels inside the bundle DASH pushes; pushing a bundle is the install verb, which needs the helper. On 2026-08-08 DASH authenticated to a real sshd with its own minted key and the host answered 'bash: line 1: status: command not found'. The answer is one snippet a person pastes before DASH has any way in, generated by the new pure lib/host-bootstrap.ts and returned by a new audited command, host.setup (mutates: false - it reads DASH's own public key and the helper this build ships, and composes a string). VERB RESOLUTION IS DECIDED AND RECORDED (acceptance bar 3): FORCED COMMAND, not namespaced verbs. The allowed-keys line is restrict,command="/opt/orchestratedash/dash-host" <key>. Namespacing (dash-status) solves the collision of English words on PATH and nothing else - the key would still be a general shell credential. command= solves it by removing the question (no PATH entries at all) and does what namespacing cannot: ADR 0007's promise that DASH chooses which operation, never what to run, was about DASH's own code being unable to compose a command and said nothing about what the key could do in other hands. sshd runs the helper whatever the client asks, so a key exfiltrated from this machine cannot open a shell there. restrict does the boring half - no port forwarding, agent forwarding, X11, pty or user rc - and is the switch rather than a hand-written list so whatever OpenSSH adds next release is off too. See ADR 0009. THE SEAM THAT COST: sshd invokes a forced command with NO ARGUMENTS, so entry.ts - which read process.argv - now reads SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND through a new pure helperArgv(argv, original). Argv still wins when present, so every existing caller and the local-child fixture proof behave exactly as before. The variable is split on whitespace and handed to the same checkDeployRequest as everything else; there is no shell between the two, and more than a verb plus one identifier is REFUSED rather than truncated. tests/deploy-bridge.test.ts now spawns the REAL BUILT HELPER with empty argv and only SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND set, and gets {ok:true,verb:'status',bundles:[]} - the same answer the attended run finally got by hand, reached without a single argument. Whether an agent can be sent anywhere is a fact about DASH's own folder for it and needs no network, but the only way to learn it was to choose a server and read what came back -- and in main that refusal sits AFTER the host-key gate, so somebody with an unconfirmed server was told about the server and never told the agent could not have gone either way. AgentDeployView is that fact on the view (AgentRow and WorkspaceView both carry it, built by agentDeployStanding from inspectAgentFolderStanding). It is NOT the gate: produceAgentFolderBundle refuses again in main and stays the authority, the arrangement the add-a-server form's duplicate check already has. What it buys is that nobody is offered a control that was never going to work -- the server card disables the button and says MANIFEST_ONLY_DEPLOY_REFUSAL the moment a migrated agent is chosen, and the agent's own page renders the refusal and NO control at all, because a greyed-out picker of servers puts the reason next to a control about servers. It never says nothing was changed on a failed deploy -- produce, install and start run behind one answer and DASH cannot tell which stopped, so the next action sends the person to the machine that knows. And it never renders the server's report while a push is still going, because the previous check's count under 'putting it there' answers the question the person is waiting on with the previous one. No commit is claimed: the packet is part of the commit, so a pre-merge entry cannot name its own hash. WHAT THIS IS: the unit of the Connections page changes and the content does not. Henrik's two verdicts are one layer apart -- MAR-383's checklist 'makes no sense to me right now', and MAR-533's rebuild of it 'cluttered and a lot of text' -- and both are the same fault, a page organised by DASH's own bookkeeping rather than by a service somebody recognises. The ruling: THE CONNECTOR IS THE UNIT THAT GETS CONNECTED, THE AGENT IS THE UNIT THAT NEEDS IT. So the page is tiles, one per service, each naming the agents that depend on it, and MAR-533's capability card is the RECEIPT ONE CLICK AWAY -- the same component, the same three-party drawing, the same nobody-asked-for-this list, the same wider-permission banner and usage history, rendered inside the disclosure. Nothing honest is removed; what changes is which question the page opens on. THE GROUPING KEY IS THE PROVIDER, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. `google-gmail` is one authorization server, one client, one consent screen; `connection_id` beside it is a string each author chose, and the shipped Gmail example calls it `gmail` while nothing stops the next author calling it `mail`. Keying on ids would draw two Gmail tiles and reintroduce the duplicate this page exists to kill. A test drives exactly that case and the screenshot harness seeds it. CONNECT ONCE, AND IT REALLY IS ONCE. This is the half that is not a view change and it was Henrik's explicit call on 2026-08-09 after the session put three options to him. Grants are keyed per agent (`dash.connection.{agent}.{connection}.{field}`), so before this two agents needing Gmail meant two trips through Google's consent screen -- and lib/oauth/providers.ts sets prompt=consent deliberately, so the second trip was a real one. `findGrantSharers` and `shareGrant` in lib/connection-actions.ts write one received consent to every agent that named the provider AND independently qualified for it: every candidate goes through `resolveCredentialTarget`, the same gate the direct path uses, so a sharer is an agent that would have been allowed to run this exact sign-in itself. Each gets its own vault entry, its own masked reference and its own receipt resolved from its OWN manifest -- which is what keeps this out of broker semantics: what the broker later resolves for a shared agent is indistinguishable from a grant it received directly, because it is one. Revocation stays per agent. An agent that asked for more than the consent covered still reads `not_issued` on the extras, which is the state MAR-533 built for. WHAT THE FAN-OUT WILL NOT DO: only OAuth. A typed secret is a value a person handed DASH for a named agent, with no consent screen and no scopes, and copying it elsewhere would be DASH redistributing something given for one purpose. `describeSharedGrant` promises exactly this much and no more, and a test drives an API-key tile asserting the page stays silent. The `listAgentIds` dependency is optional and its ABSENCE MEANS NO FAN-OUT rather than an error, so every caller built before this connects exactly the agent it named. THE DISCLOSURE IS BEFORE THE BUTTON, and a render test asserts it by POSITION rather than by presence -- 'somewhere on the card' is satisfied by a sentence underneath the thing it was supposed to warn about. It is ADR 0002 amendment 2's rule applied to the one consequence in DASH that lands on an agent the person is not looking at. `also_connects` is on the view rather than derived by a page, so the tile and the receipt card cannot come to disagree with the fan-out that actually happens. THREE DEFECTS THE SCREENSHOTS FOUND, none of which a test was looking for. (1) Tile order was first-appearance, which is agent order, which is alphabetical -- so a store whose first agent was `invoice-reviewer` opened the page on two tiles DASH cannot connect and pushed Gmail below the fold. Tiles a person can act on now come first, as a stable partition rather than a sort, so nothing reorders under the cursor when something connects. (2) The summary counted a tile as shared if several agents named it, so a model-provider tile DASH holds none of made the page say 'you connect each once' about a thing there is nothing to connect; it now counts by the same rule the disclosure uses. (3) The shared tile's own Sign in button sat below a 900px fold, under two stacked bordered notes -- the disclosure was tightened from six lines to three with every claim kept, and `describeProof`'s `cannot` sentence became prose instead of a second box. It is unchanged, verbatim and still announced as a note; it stops competing with the one consequence a person must read before pressing. Prop-stamped onto the audited stills, never whole-canvas regeneration - PixelLab animate_image drifted the characters +/-2px with off-palette pixels, so props are PixelLab designs on a forced palette and the audit measures costume-never-status: every frame outside the declared prop box is a byte copy of the still, sheets pin the sha256 of their source still, no frame paints emerald. brand:check extended (auditSheet/checkActions re-derive the box from pixels). Henrik 2026-08-09: keep these sprites for now; ninja and wizard fine, knight not tight - production artwork pass later. PHASE B MERGED 2026-08-10 via PR #114 (4719ea6), from branch 000henrik/mar-587-phase-b cut from origin/master at 0048a37. WHAT THIS IS: every fleet card draws its character at 200px, and where a sheet exists the character performs its idle action - the knight swings, the ninja tosses a shuriken, the wizard throws a fireball. Henrik 2026-08-09: 'to make the fleet look more like a game and character selection.' COSTUME FLAVOUR, NEVER STATUS - AND IT IS THE SHAPE OF THE CODE RATHER THAN A PROMISE. actionFor's only argument is the character, which is itself assigned once at creation from a seed and never recomputed from state, so there is no parameter a status could arrive through. Three of eleven characters have sheets; the eight without draw the audited still exactly as before - no stand-in loop and no reordering to put the animated ones first, which would have turned DASH's asset library into something a reader tries to read as a ranking. The call site is fenced from the other end: checkCostume now fails action={...} for anything that is not a literal, and unlike the name={...} rule it is exact rather than heuristic, because whether a surface animates is a decision about the surface taken once in the source and never a fact about an agent. MAR-586's glance chips carry every meaning on the card and were neither restyled nor moved; the harness asserts per frame that the portrait sits above them. --motion-idle IS A NEW TOKEN AND NOT A REUSE OF --motion-beckon. app/tokens.css's own comment says its five cycle lengths are motion that IS state; this loop is the exact opposite, so it gets its own name. It carries 1800ms, the number beckon carries today, and is still separate: beckon is the rhythm of 'a decision is waiting on you' and exists to be tuned until it reads from across the room, and a shared token would let that tuning silently re-time every costume in the fleet - or stop the tuning happening because it would. 1800ms over 8 audited frames is 225ms a frame, which is what docs/mar-587-o-actions-preview.html was reviewed at. Because it is a token, reduced motion needs no rule in app/globals.css: 0ms leaves the sprite on its base background-position, which is frame 0 - the character standing with its prop. That was measured rather than assumed and was the one thing that could plausibly have gone the other way (a zero-duration steps() parking on the END of the sheet would have drawn a blank box). 200, AND NOT 150. OSize gains one member: 4x the 50px source, because image-rendering: pixelated upscales by nearest neighbour and anything between whole multiples lands some source pixels on two screen pixels and some on three. 150 is a legal multiple and is deliberately absent - a size is in the union because a surface draws at it, the same argument the size prop makes for having no default - and MAR-586 had already answered 'bigger' with 100 before this ask came. BOUNDED, AND STOPPED WHEN NOBODY IS LOOKING. steps() over background-position is eight repaints per 1800ms cycle, no JavaScript per frame, no timer, and deliberately no will-change (which would promote every card in the fleet to its own compositor layer to save repaints steps() has already removed). There is no media query for 'the window is hidden', so one listener in app/layout.tsx writes data-window=hidden on the root and the stylesheet pauses every loop under it - in the layout rather than beside the sprites because visibility is a fact about the window, and a fleet of twelve agents would otherwise register twelve listeners for one document-wide fact. It deliberately does NOT claim a merely unfocused or partly covered window: those are still visible and their fleet still moves. THE TYPED VIEW IS HELD TO THE AUDIT RECORD. lib/brand/o-actions.ts stands to o-actions.json as o-cast.ts stands to o-cast.json, and checkActionModule is new: the manifest is 233 lines of per-frame pixel counts that exist to be measured rather than shipped, so the renderer compiles against a typed array and the check fails any drift between them. The failure it exists for is quiet - re-vendor a fourth sheet, add it to the manifest, forget the array, and everything passes while the character simply never animates with no line anywhere saying why. EVIDENCE: qa-screenshots-mar587/ from electron/capture-actions.ts, a new store-seeding harness on capture-glance.ts's terms and for a reason of its own: an agent's character is a HASH OF ITS NAME, so a run against whatever store a machine holds photographs whichever costumes that machine happens to wear. It seeds five agents whose names were chosen to land on a scene - budget-digest (knight), deal-finder (medic), ledger-notes (ninja), news-scout (explorer), uptime-sorter (wizard) - which is also the order agentsView sorts them into: animated, still, animated, still, animated. Each carries one of MAR-586's five answers so the images show the chips in place rather than only the costume. A DEFECT FOUND IN SOMETHING ELSE AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: the 375px fleet grid scrolls sideways by 24px, and it is MAR-586's rather than this issue's. The harness now names what overflows; at 375 it is ol.row-list.fleet-grid (24px, overflow-x visible) inside main (8px, auto). The cause is minmax(19rem, 1fr) - a fixed 304px track floor against a container about 280px wide once the sidebar rail and page padding are taken - and it is independent of the portrait by construction, since a track minimum that is a length does not consult its contents. 200px of sprite fits the 280px that is there. Left rather than fixed because the floor is a recorded MAR-586 decision with a stated reason, and the one-line encoding that keeps the reason while removing the overflow (minmax(min(19rem, 100%), 1fr)) belongs to whoever owns it. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: verify:shell did not run on this machine (see proof.run). Nothing here was seen on a real machine's own data - the store is a scratch directory the run seeded, so the frames are evidence of what the fleet draws for a given store and evidence about nobody's actual machine.

issues.note: MERGED 2026-08-09 via PR #107 (16e6cfd), coordinator-resolved against MAR-582: both sessions authored migration 12; ai_key_checks keeps 12 (installed databases recorded it), agent_looks renumbered to 13, user_version 14. Fleet cards answer four recorded questions - new output (agent_looks last-looked), needs approval, lacks connections (MAR-569 resolution), stale vs own schedule - no invented meters per the MAR-547 ruling. PLANNED, on branch 000henrik/mar-586-fleet-glance cut from origin/master at 9f7b306. No commit named here for MAR-577 reason: the packet is part of the commit and a pre-merge entry cannot name its own hash. WHAT THIS IS: every fleet card now answers Henriks four questions -- has it new output, does it need approval, does it lack connections, is it stale -- plus a real button to the agent page. MAR-547 ruling governs it: every chip is a recorded fact and there is no invented meter anywhere in it. THE ONE NEW FACT. Three of the four were already recorded and are derived at render time; the fourth needed a last-looked timestamp per agent, which is the only thing this stores. agent_looks is its own table rather than a column on agents, for the reason evidence_pulls is one -- it records something the READER did, not something an agent did, and a column would sit inside the row importManifest rewrites on every re-import, where the next ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE would either have to remember to leave it alone (the trap avatar own note describes) or quietly reset it. Migration 12, IF NOT EXISTS on the hosts migration terms. WRITTEN BY A COMMAND, NEVER BY A READ. lib/shell/read.ts states that a read changes nothing and is therefore unaudited, and view.workspace is polled every five seconds while a run is going -- so recording a look inside that answer would have rewritten the fact by the window staying open rather than by anybody arriving. glance.looked is a sixth command family and the only one in the catalogue about the person at the keyboard. Payload is one agent id and deliberately no time: main stamps its own clock, so page script cannot mark an agent as read at a moment it chose and silence its card for good. ONE DEFINITION OF LATE. MAR-441 arithmetic was lifted out of deriveStatus into pastScheduleExpectation and shared rather than copied; a card and a status field that disagreed about whether the same agent was late would be worse than either being wrong. Measured against DASH own record of runs rather than the snapshot last_activity_at, because MAR-586 asks about RUNS and because DASH runs table outlives the process. Two refusals: a run happening now (asked of both records), and an agent the person paused. THE CONNECTION COUNT IS MAR-569 RESOLUTION WHERE THERE IS ONE. resolveRequirements against connectionRowsFor, which was extracted from connectionsView so both callers share one row builder rather than forking the four standings. Where an author declared no requirements block -- which is every agent on any real machine today -- the declared agent_dom.connections checklist answers instead, on panelDocument folder-first rule: the newer finer document wins and the older one keeps answering for everything exported before it. A row DASH cannot hold a credential for is deliberately not counted: DASH offers no button for it and a chip would send a person to do something DASH can never mark as done. CLICKABILITY. Each chip links to the place that answers it -- three to sections of the agent page, the connections one to the Connection Center, because what an agent needs connected is that page subject while the agent own Connections section is the AGENT report on connections it already has. The agent page now honours the fragment it arrives with: a browser resolves one against a page whose content has not crossed the IPC boundary yet, so without that effect the link landed people at the top and left them looking. HENRIK MID-SESSION on the first screenshots: I want the fleet cards to fit like 3 in a row. And the avatar to be bigger. So the fleet takes the concept fleet_monitor composition -- header band, portrait on a tinted tile, controls along the bottom -- on a fleet-grid modifier rather than a change to the .row-list the Runs and Connections pages share. auto-fit with a floor, not repeat(3, 1fr): three-in-a-row is what 1280px gets and a 375px phone gets one column rather than three it cannot read. issues.note: MERGED 2026-08-10 via PR #112 (e29fa19). No commit named here for MAR-577's reason: the packet is part of the commit and a pre-merge entry cannot name its own hash. WHAT THIS IS: an outside AI (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) edits the folder DASH keeps for one agent, and DASH notices, says what changed in plain sentences, refuses an invalid edit with the schema's own error, and accepts the change only when a person presses accept. DETECTION IS A BUTTON, NOT A WATCHER, and the argument is provenance rather than cost: an editor saves twenty times while it works, and the interesting moment is 'I am finished, tell me what you would be accepting'. FOLDER_CHECK_COPY.detail says out loud that DASH is not watching, because an app that quietly looks and an app that does not are indistinguishable on screen until it matters. THE SILENT SWAP WAS ALREADY HAPPENING, IN TWO PLACES, AND BOTH ARE FIXED. (1) views/build.ts panelDocument read the folder on every five-second poll while title, goal, permissions and input roles came from the row -- so an outside edit moved half the agent page immediately and said nothing. It now reads the row, which is DASH's projection of the folder AS ACCEPTED. (2) reconcileAgentFolders projected any differing folder over the row at every startup; it now projects only when the folder still hashes to the registration's manifest_sha256 -- index drift after a crash is a repair, an external edit is a proposal. An edit is deliberately NOT recorded as a folder issue, because describeStoreDamage renders every one of those as store damage and tells the person to re-import. THE HEADLINE SENTENCE NEEDED BOTH HALVES. Henrik's example -- 'adds 2 sources and changes the schedule' -- spans two files: sources live in code/sources.json (lib/agent-sources.ts) and the schedule is agent_dom.trigger. Manifest-only detection would have reported 'no changes' on the exact scenario the issue names. THE BASELINE IS NEW STORED DATA AND HAD TO BE. files_sha256 is hashed over DECLARED handoff paths and cannot be recomputed from a folder (a project's agent.mjs and its code/agent.mjs are stored at the same place), so the registration now also carries accepted_files -- per stored path, per digest -- plus accepted_sources, the source NAMES, because the folder holds only the current copy of a file and 'which sources were added' cannot be answered by re-reading it. Absent means no baseline, which is its own reported state and never 'nothing changed'. THE DETECTOR READS ONLY THE RECORDED PATHS AND NEVER WALKS. The sample agent writes into code/reports/ and code/runs/, inside the folder a walk would enumerate, so a walk would report an agent's own work as somebody's edit on the flagship agent every check. The honest cost -- a file an editor ADDS is not reported -- is stated to the person, not just in a header. THE SENTENCE THAT WAS FALSE AND IS NOW TRUE. FOLDER_CHANGED first said 'DASH is still running the version you approved'. It is not: the runner's cwd is that folder (handoff-flow.ts) and nothing verifies its contents before spawning, so changed instructions run at the next run either way. The card says that, and adopt_detail says what accepting IS for -- bringing DASH's description into line with the folder. Same distinction ADR 0003 draws about network: read. ACCEPT DOES NOT GO THROUGH importManifest, and that is not an optimisation. That door stages a complete replacement folder and swaps it in, deleting anything not re-declared -- including code/reports/, which for the sample agent is everything it has ever produced. acceptFolderManifest updates the row and nothing else; the person's editor already wrote the bytes. Same two gates (schema, then checkManifestConstraints), so an edit refused at the front door is refused here in the same words. THE INVALID PATH REUSES explainImportFailure VERBATIM: DASH's headline and suggestion over the validator's own raw errors, so a folder edit and a first import fail in one vocabulary. ADR 0010 IS NEW AND REVERSES HALF OF A STATED RULE. MAR-574 wrote 'DASH keeps no record of what it has deployed where'. The reasoning -- no inventory of somebody else's machine -- is kept and is still why host.probe returns a count and not names; what it got wrong was forbidding DASH to remember its OWN act. agent_deploys (migration 14) holds agent, host, sent_at and the two digests of what went across, and will never hold a running column. Every sentence derived from it is past tense and every one of them ends by saying DASH has not asked the server. host.forget deletes the rows, because after the label is gone a row could only render as an orphaned claim. SEVENTH COMMAND FAMILY: folder.check (mutates false), folder.adopt (mutates true), folder.reveal (mutates false, no path crosses the boundary in either direction). check and adopt are two commands rather than one precisely so nothing can compare-then-apply in a single call. EVIDENCE: qa-screenshots-mar584/{unchanged,changed,invalid,behind}/ -- 108 packaged-renderer frames, all from the real shell with the real Check for changes button pressed per frame, at three widths in both themes and both densities. electron/capture-folder.ts is a new store-seeding harness on capture-deploy.ts's terms. Its own witness caught two real defects: the first run used the v1 example manifest, which has no agent_dom, so the schedule half of the headline sentence was silently absent; and the invalid card's next action said 'listed below' while the validator block renders above it. WHAT IS NOT PROVEN: verify:shell did not run on this machine -- the smoke exited before any proof because orphan Electron processes held the app's single-instance lock, and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing them, so CI's Windows shell-smoke is this branch's installed witness. No real outside editor was used: the scenes' edits were written by the harness, which costs nothing about the surface (DASH compares bytes and cannot tell which editor wrote them) but should not be read as photographs of a Claude Code session. No push to a real server: the behind scene's deploy row is a real agent_deploys record with genuinely disagreeing digests, written directly, because a real push needs MAR-489's attended run.

issues.note: MERGED 2026-08-10 via PR #117 (04a19a5). MAR-583's DASH half; the MCP half is merged (OrchestrateKIT-MCP 3abe6e9, ADR-MAR-583) and emits planned_route[].default_model_level per AI-needing step. JUDGMENTS: docs/adr/0011-which-model-an-agent-uses.md. THE MIRROR, MAR-555/578 MECHANICS: the optional closed enum in agent.manifest.v2.schema.json, the typed property in lib/contracts.ts, and lib/ai/model-levels.ts as the pure reader beside the schema (no imports, vocabulary by value, reachable from the renderer chunk Ajv cannot be). tests/model-levels.test.ts runs one corpus through both and requires the same verdict. contract.lock.json UNTOUCHED: it locks the frozen telemetry v1 pair and v2 was never in it. NO FALLBACK TO model_tier, deliberately: that mapping is ADR-MAR-583's table and a second copy in DASH would be the one nobody updates. An agent exported before the emitter therefore gets no per-step choice, DASH says so, and re-exporting is the fix. THE RECOMMENDED SETTING HAS NO ROW. Three tables (migration 15), all empty for an agent nobody configured; choosing the default back DELETES rather than storing it, because a stored copy of a manifest's answer goes stale the moment its author publishes. NOT ONE OF THE THREE HAS A COST COLUMN. THE CATALOGUE IS NEVER STORED. ai_key_checks still records a count and never a list (ADR 0002 invariant 7): probeModelProvider gained wantIds defaulting to the narrow answer, classifyProbe drops the ids, and the list lives in the page's state. tests/model-choice.test.ts searches the whole SQLite file for the scripted ids, so a future column, blob or cache would all fail it. The list is a button rather than an automatic load because the agent page polls every five seconds. THE CORRECTION THIS SLICE MADE TO ITS OWN CLAIM, found by a test fixture: TELEMETRY V1 HAS CARRIED `model` ON EVERY RUN EVENT SINCE THE CONTRACT WAS FROZEN AND NOTHING IN DASH HAD EVER DRAWN IT. So a run now carries two kinds of fact in ADR 0005's shape - DASH's own setting at first sight of the run (something DASH did) and the run's own report (something DASH was told) - the report wins on the label, the detail names its source, the run_models row is written once and never revised, and a disagreement between the two is REPORTED rather than resolved. cost_usd sits on the same event and is DELIBERATELY STILL UNREAD; a test asserts over the source that nothing reads it, because MAR-299 owns spend and needs an answer to whose number it is. DEPLOY: the choice travels as a generated data/models/{agent}.json beside the generated registration and never inside agent/ (that tree is the author's byte-for-byte and MAR-584 hashes exactly those paths). A bundle is REFUSED OUTRIGHT when the plan needs a model and the agent asks DASH to hold the key for it - DASH does not send keys to servers. The check is on the shape of the arrangement, not on the vault's current contents, so the outcome is predictable. An agent managing its own key is not refused. THE GENERAL CASE (any dash_managed connection on an agent going to a server) IS NOT FIXED HERE and is named rather than half-solved. EIGHTH COMMAND FAMILY: model.choose, model.step, model.list. The renderer names an agent, a connection and a field and never a provider, an origin, a path or a key; the one value it supplies from a provider's answer - a model id - is re-checked with isModelId in main rather than trusted for having come from a list DASH made. EVIDENCE: qa-screenshots-mar583/ - 24 packaged-renderer frames, four states at 375/768/1280 in both themes, harness reporting 0 overflowing frames, 0 without the section, 0 where the recommended option was not first, 0 showing an amount. electron/capture-models.ts caught three real defects before an image was reviewed: every seeded manifest refused (a full set of photographs of a page saying it had no such agent), 'Connect a OpenRouter key' at every width, and a disabled control at full contrast with its longest option truncated mid-word. NOT PROVEN: NO REAL MODEL PROVIDER HAS BEEN CONTACTED. The capture harness writes a connection_secrets row with a masked hint and puts NO KEY IN THE VAULT, so pressing 'See what OpenRouter offers' in those images would fail and the harness does not press it; the list path is driven against a scripted probe in tests and against a real loopback server in MAR-582's suite. verify:shell DID NOT RUN locally - other worktrees' Electron instances were live and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing them - so CI's Windows shell-smoke is this branch's installed witness. NO COMPLETION CALL, no streaming, no embedding, and ZERO CHANGES UNDER runner/: MAR-582's boundary stands, choosing a model is now possible and nothing in DASH yet sends a prompt to one, and nothing reads the deployed data/models file.

issues.note: MERGED 2026-08-10 via PR #121 (be90d84). The agent-page conversation, answering from the agent's own saved reports. JUDGMENTS: docs/adr/0012-talking-to-an-agent.md. THE BOUNDARY MAR-582 WROTE DOWN IS CROSSED, and its two conditions are split: this builds the cost story and NOT the per-run budget, which is exactly why an agent cannot reach a completion. SPENDING IS A THIRD ACCESS KIND: BrokerAccess gains `spend`, the three completions live in their own frozen SPEND_PATHS, and WRITE_PATHS IS UNTOUCHED and still one Gmail path -- the array a reader is invited to treat as the complete answer to 'what can this application do to my account?' did not grow because a feature started spending money. A third variant made every switch over access stop compiling, which is how grant.ts, connection-card.ts, connections.ts and views/build.ts were made to decide what a spend looks like on a card. A COMPLETION RUNS WHEN A PERSON ASKS: broker.handle takes a REQUIRED origin ('agent' | 'person'), a spend is refused for 'agent' with the new needs_a_person code BEFORE THE VAULT IS TOUCHED, and the value is decided by which function read the request rather than by anything in it -- the drain loop passes 'agent' for every line off a child's stdout whatever it contains. No default, because neither value is safe to default to. It gates spending and nothing else. WHOSE NUMBER IS THIS, ANSWERED -- the question MAR-583 said had to be settled before anything read cost_usd: every figure with a currency symbol DASH shows was stated by somebody else and the sentence beside it says who. NO PRICE TABLE, no multiplication of a token count. OpenRouter's own charge is quoted and named; Anthropic and OpenAI state none so DASH shows what was read and written plus one sentence saying so; and telemetry v1's cost_usd on a run event is THE AGENT'S figure about its own past, attributed in as many words -- ADR 0005's two kinds of fact, about money, side by side. The estimate before a question is a CEILING DASH SET ITSELF plus what questions here have already cost, quoted; a first question shows no amount and says why. MAR-583's assertion was NOT deleted: the model surface still must carry no amount, and a second test names every file whose code touches the field. A LEVEL SAYS HOW STRONG, NEVER WHICH: an agent on match-each-step has no model name, so the chat is unavailable, says so, and points at the picker one section down -- DASH does not choose somebody's model and does not invent a level-to-name mapping to avoid asking. It does hand over MAR-583's own argument: answering from saved reports is summarising, the cheapest kind of step. THE ANSWER DRIVES NOTHING, which is the boundary rather than the system prompt: nothing in DASH reads an answer -- not parsed, no link followed out of it, no command derived, no approval resolved, and it reaches no agent. The citation list comes from DASH's OWN record of the items it selected, so a model that invents a source cannot make it appear beside the answer. TENTH COMMAND FAMILY: ask.question, the first entry in the catalogue that costs money and the first with irreversible:true for a reason that is not an effect in the world. The renderer names an agent, a connection, a field and a question -- NEVER a model, which main reads from the model.choose row. MIGRATION 18, agent_questions: the whole question and the whole answer are stored, which broker_audit deliberately does not do for an agent's inputs -- the reasoning inverts because a person typed these words into something shaped like a conversation. It is the one table in DASH with a cost column, and MAR-583's three still have none: amount_usd is written ONLY from a figure a provider stated inside the reply it charged for. SUPERSEDES MAR-299's non-goal 'no direct model calls from DASH', which was written when DASH was a monitor. MAR-588 inbound and MAR-585 reuse this surface and may not relax the origin gate without the per-run budget. ONE OUTCOME WORTH KNOWING: a provider that answered and charged, whose row DASH then failed to write, is reported as answer_lost -- the person is out of pocket with nothing to show for it, so 'it did not work' would be false about the charge and the sentence says they were charged.

WHAT THIS IS: a connection becomes a fleet-level thing -- an account or a key the person gave DASH, recorded against a provider, existing with no agent present -- and an agent's grant becomes a materialization of it. THE BROKER WAS NOT TOUCHED, and that is the safety argument rather than a convenience: lib/broker/execute.ts computes the same per-agent vault name it always has, so 'indistinguishable at the boundary' is a property of not editing the read path. ADR 0002's three parties are all still in the same hands -- DASH built the operation, THE AGENT'S OWN MANIFEST declared the scopes, the person granted them at the provider. THE ONE NEW AUTHORITY IS DERIVED: a fleet sign-in has no manifest, so DASH decides what to ask for, and the answer is the union of required_scopes over its own operation table -- which makes 'DASH never asks for a scope no operation uses' true by construction. AN AGENT IMPORTED AFTERWARDS IS NOT CONNECTED SILENTLY: it is named on the card as waiting with one button (fleet.share) that gives it the consent DASH already holds, asking for nothing and contacting nobody. issues.note: MERGED 2026-08-12 via PR #163 (30e5ffa). Worktree ../dash-mar626 off master 4f0bc56 (after PRs #160/#161). Henrik's report: a fresh, untouched scaffold of a sample agent refused to deploy to Hostinger over a model-provider connection it had never connected - MAR-619's News Scout declares that connection `optional: true` on purpose, and the gate refused anyway. Root cause: lib/deploy/connection-travel.ts's assessConnectionTravel asked the manifest whether a run needs a connection (a declaration, or planNeedsAModel reading model_tier off the plan) and never asked whether DASH actually holds a credential for it - so `target.kind === "provider_key" && needsAModel` forced `run_needs_it` regardless of the declared `optional: true` and regardless of whether anything was ever connected. Every new sample agent declares a model requirement now, so every new agent was undeployable. FIX: assessConnectionTravel takes a third argument, `held: readonly HeldCredential[]` (the `connection_secrets` rows for this agent - `{connection_id, field_id}`, structurally satisfied by both `lib/secret-refs.ts`'s SecretReference and `lib/connection-actions.ts`'s heldCredentials, no reshaping needed at either call site). A connectable field the vault holds nothing for is skipped before it ever reaches the refuse/warn decision - nothing held means nothing DASH is withholding from the server, so there is nothing to strand, regardless of what the manifest declares or of whether a fleet connector's own key exists (fleetReach in lib/fleet/grants.ts writes into the same connection_secrets table when it materializes a credential, so one lookup covers both a direct connect and a fleet-materialized one). MERGED 2026-08-13 via PR #180 (f9e18c8). MERGED, NOT PROVEN: ADR 0020 explicitly proves nothing — no MCP server was connected, no agent called a tool, no client was implemented, and the ADR carries a section saying so. PLANNED, PR OPEN 2026-08-13. PR #180 (branch 000henrik/mar-633-mcp-client), worktree ../dash-mar633, cut from origin/master at 90d95c6 and reconciled onto eaeb56b (PR #179's promotion of MAR-630/624/620) before review; the only conflict was this file's own header and the MAR-620 note, resolved by taking master's promoted note. ADR-FIRST BY INSTRUCTION: docs/adr/0020-an-mcp-server-is-a-connection-dash-brokers.md landed as its own commit f6fc90e before any code, and lib/mcp/ landed second as 681586e. THE DECISION: DASH is the MCP client; an MCP server is a connection and an MCP tool is a broker operation DASH did not write. That last clause is what the ADR turns on - every operation in lib/broker/operations.ts is a literal a human typed, which is where WRITE_PATHS gets its claim to be the complete answer to what the application can do to an account. A tool arrives from a third party, so the frozen thing moves: the pinned set is the admitted tool set of one server, fixed at consent, and notifications/tools/list_changed becomes a consent event. A server may narrow without asking and may never widen without a person. The cheap alternative - one generic mcp.call passthrough operation - is rejected explicitly, because it would leave the array looking unchanged while making every claim built on it false. TRANSPORT: remote Streamable HTTP first; the deprecated HTTP+SSE pair is not implemented. stdio is an install rather than a connection, and the argument is deliberately not that it runs local code (DASH spawns agents already): an agent has a folder, a panel and a run history while a server spawned for a tool call has none; npx -y is a run-time download nobody can describe at consent; and the blast radius is DASH own user account (home directory, ADR 0007 SSH keys, .env files, the DASH store) rather than a provider account. When stdio arrives it needs an absolute path to a program already on disk, pinned by digest, launchers refused by name, and A MANIFEST MAY ASK FOR A SERVER AND MAY NEVER SUPPLY THE COMMAND - the one rule whose absence turns a connection kind into remote code execution arriving through the import door. CURATION: membership rule borrowed verbatim from CONNECTOR_KINDS_V1 - a server is in the catalogue because DASH connected it, listed its tools, classified them and wrote the sentences. Explicitly NOT a safety claim; DASH cannot audit a remote server behaviour. Add-your-own is a different register rather than a riskier one, because for an unknown server the only text available is the server own, so third-party text is quoted and attributed and never rendered as DASH description. Prompt injection starts on the consent screen, not in the run. CONSENT: per server AND per tool class, intersected in ADR 0002 amendment 1 three-party shape with the third party replaced (DASH classified it / the manifest asked for it / the person ticked the class). Classes stay read|write|spend - no send class, because a sent message is a write whose consequence says it cannot be recalled - plus one modifier MCP forces that the existing vocabulary cannot say: reaches_beyond_server, for a tool acting at an address the agent names. CLASSIFICATION NEVER READS ToolAnnotations: the specification says clients should never make critical tool-use decisions on annotations from untrusted servers, and MCP own schema defaults (destructiveHint true, openWorldHint true) agree with the conservative reading. An unclassified tool is not a read, it is attended-only - ADR 0019 move applied to a new substrate. INJECTION: content is data. The ADR separates what DASH enforces structurally (a result cannot become a broker request, cannot widen an admission, cannot open a spend allowance - allowRunSpend is called only by electron/main.ts on a Run press) from what it cannot enforce (the agent own reasoning), and states the second plainly rather than claiming to prevent injection. The half that can be closed is the READ-THEN-REACH RULE: a successful brokered MCP read marks the run, and any subsequent write, spend or reaches_beyond_server call in that run refuses needs_a_person unless a person approves that specific call. Four limits are stated in the docblock and tested: per run not per agent; no distinction between safe and hostile content; it stops brokered egress after a brokered read AND NOTHING ELSE (not the agent own report, artifact or digest); and it is not a defence against injection, only against a persuaded agent reaching a consequence unattended. TWO FINDINGS THE DECISION SURFACED. (1) token_custodian is singular and the fact is a pair: MCP authorization requires RFC 8707 resource indicators, so the token DASH holds is audience-bound to the MCP server and cannot be replayed against whatever the server fronts - which makes DASH vault custody correct rather than a compromise - while the server own upstream credential stays the server and a disconnect does not withdraw it. Either sentence alone misleads, so describeMcpCustody returns two named fields. (2) An input-schema digest catches the rename-preserving widening a name check misses: search(query) becoming search(query, exfiltrate_to) is the same name, the same class and a different tool. REMOTE PARITY WAITS ON MAR-629, by instruction and on the merits: a deployed agent emits broker requests and the broker is in DASH, so an MCP call from a host is answered only while DASH is open and settles at the agent own broker_unavailable timeout - ADR 0002 amendment 1 stated cost, not a new defect. Two of MAR-629 three candidates change the answer here and one does not, so picking would commit MCP before the credential question is settled. Two things ARE decided because they hold under every candidate: no surface may say a deployed agent can use an MCP server until MAR-629 lands, and a stdio MCP server on a VPS is agent_managed under ADR 0006 whatever MAR-629 decides. WHAT SHIPPED IN CODE: lib/mcp/ as pure modules with no I/O, tested the way tests/broker-threat-model.test.ts tests operations - transport.ts (admission, permanent stdio rules checked ahead of the temporary gate so a well-formed stdio proposal refuses on stdio_not_admitted alone while a manifest command, a launcher and a relative path each refuse on their own ground; RFC 8707 resource derived from the URL keeping the path so two servers on one host do not share an audience), catalogue.ts (CATALOGUE_SERVERS EMPTY AND PINNED BY VALUE because nobody has connected a server, with checkCatalogueEntry invariants and a DASH_MCP_PROOF_URL loopback-only proof entry in loopbackProofOrigin shape so the machinery is testable before the first real entry), tools.ts (names get parseBrokerRequest discipline because they reach broker_audit and a newline-delimited protocol; descriptions refused rather than repaired; annotations kept under a name that says whose claim they are; canonical-JSON sha256 schema digests), admission.ts (three-party intersection, exclusions reported under the party a person can act on, diffAdmission writes no grant), reach.ts (the rule and its bounded ledger, whose eviction direction is the unsafe one and is stated rather than hidden), result.ts (WHITELIST of block kinds rather than a stripper, byte-capped on a UTF-8 boundary, javascript:/file: URIs carried but never openable, provenance on every result), audit.ts (NO NEW TABLE - an MCP call is a broker_audit row whose operation is mcp.<server>.<tool>, unambiguous because a server id may not contain a dot, refusing to mint an id past the broker protocol own 128-character limit; field names and never values; account_hint null because a server token identifies nobody, the same null MAR-582 writes for a keyed grant), card.ts (both custody sentences, attributed third-party text, plain-language copy asserted by the shared expectPlainLanguage helper). EVIDENCE: pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm brand:check green; pnpm state:check valid; focused vitest 4 files / 72 passed; full suite 174 files / 3375 passed / 11 skipped / 0 failed; CI run 31746135687 green on 681586e. verify:shell NOT RUN - a parallel lane was live on this machine and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing Electron; nothing in this change reaches the shell, since lib/mcp/ performs no I/O and has no caller yet, so CI Windows shell-smoke is the installed witness. NOT PROVEN AND DELIBERATELY SHORT OF THE ISSUE BAR: no MCP server has been connected, no agent has called a tool, no dependency was added and no client was implemented. MAR-633 asks for one real server connected through the product, its tools listed, an agent using it in a run, an audit naming the server and the tool, and a refusal a person can trigger - none of that is met, and ADR 0020 carries a section saying so in its own words so the ADR cannot be read as evidence of a working feature. SCOPE HELD: owns docs/adr/0020-*.md, lib/mcp/* and four new test files; lib/connectors.ts and every fleet file untouched (Lane 1). PR open, merge left to Henrik.

issues.note: PLANNED, on branch 000henrik/mar-657-start-an-agent, worktree ../dash-mar657 cut from origin/master at e613812 after confirming that commit is master's tip, so there is no reconciliation merge to read. PR against master. THE FINDING THAT CHANGED THE SHAPE OF THE FIX: DASH already had the verb and had never had a door. `runner.start` has been in lib/shell/ipc.ts's COMMANDS since MAR-415, carrying mutates:true/irreversible:false, mapped through RUNNER_LIFECYCLE to POST /agents/{id}/lifecycle {action:'start'} -- and its ONLY caller in the entire product was ensureRunning in lib/handoff-flow.ts, at the end of the add-agent flow. Grepping app/ for it returned nothing: no renderer surface had ever invoked it. So an agent was started on the day it was installed and by nothing afterwards. WHY EVERY AGENT WAS OFFLINE: runner/main.ts loads the registrations, constructs the Supervisor with child:null / lifecycle:'stopped' for each, and calls start on none of them -- its `supervising N registered agent(s)` line means N registrations were READ, not N processes are alive. runner/README.md states this as a deliberate non-goal ('An agent that exits stays exited. Supervision here means knows it died and says so, not brings it back'). resolveStatus then renders a registered agent with no child as `offline`, which is exactly what the real store held for competitor-scout, ai-news-scout-4 and ai-news-scout-5. Not three broken agents -- the correct rendering of a fleet nobody started. THIS IS THEREFORE A BUILD AND NOT A PROPOSAL, per the brief's own branch: starting a stopped agent is a message the runner already accepts, so no capability, route, boundary or ADR grant is new. What was missing was a preload method and a control, both in the shape runner.remove already has. ADR 0022 records the product decision anyway, because what the primary control means when there is no process is decision truth MAR-490 will have to read. ONE PRESS, NOT TWO: starting the process does not run the agent (the kit template starts idle and stays idle by design, MAR-457, and smoke proof 6d asserts it deliberately), so a control that only spawned would leave Henrik watching a status change and a second button appearing a poll later. lib/agent-start.ts performs both acts in the order electron/smoke.ts has always proved -- start, wait for the agent to publish its task, then the existing retry -- and is a function with injected ports precisely so its three outcomes and two failure modes are testable without a browser (tests/agent-start.test.ts drives all of them, including the ordering assertion that no return-value check would catch). ADR 0016 IS NOT MOVED: the spend allowance still opens in the one place it has ever opened, `input.command === 'retry'` in electron/main.ts, because the second act IS a retry going through runAgentCommand. A lifecycle press on its own still spends nothing, and the runSpend disclosure renders under the new button for the same reason it renders under Run now -- a disclosure on only one of the two buttons that spend would read as 'this one is free'. THE PREDICATE WAS NOT WIDENED, and this is the constraint the issue was most explicit about. The new branch answers a different question on a different channel: Run now asks 'is there a task to bind' and is refused by the Agent DOM pipeline; start asks 'is there a process' and is refused by the supervisor with unknown_agent|already_running|invalid_manifest|spawn_failed. already_running is excluded by the status that gates it. The gate is `offline` or `error` only -- the two statuses resolveStatus produces for a non-live child and the two SELF_REPORTABLE_STATUSES forbids an agent from claiming, so the spawn is never decided by the thing being spawned. A LATENT DEFECT FIXED BY THE BRANCH ORDER, found while placing it: runner/state.ts gates runs, choices, actions and approval_requests on the process being live, but `tasks` is the one array it does NOT gate, so a dead agent's last self-report keeps its pending waiting-to-be-run verbatim. An agent that ran and then exited therefore drew a Run now whose retry Supervisor.deliver answers with not_running -- the exact after-the-press refusal lib/views/agent-control.ts exists to prevent, arriving by the road MAR-657's own correction comment predicted. Deciding start ABOVE the pending-task check replaces a button that cannot work with one that can; tests/agent-control.test.ts asserts it directly. AGENT_CONTROL_COPY.idle's three sentences all survive untouched, with a test that a live agent with nothing pending still gets nothing_waiting and still gets no button (MAR-609's requirement, kept). ADR 0014: the label carries no machine because the local control is the permanent default that the named per-server buttons sit beside, and the machine is said in words in start_here ('DASH will start it on this computer, then ask it to run'). ADR 0010: nothing here reads agent_deploys, and the locality of the gate rests on lib/agent-dom/runner.ts's own statement that agent_dom_state 'is keyed by agent id alone -- there is exactly one row and it belongs to the copy on this computer'. HOW A SCHEDULE REACHES THE SAME DOOR (MAR-490, raised to High and linked): the verb is deliberately a composition of two routes that already existed rather than a new runner message, so a cadence needs no new one -- it fires the same two acts, in the same order, against the same routes, and the allowance opens in the same place because the second act is the same retry. What a scheduler additionally needs is what ADR 0014 already named as out of scope and did not decide: restart-on-boot, because a schedule that only fires while DASH is open is not a schedule. That is MAR-490's, not this packet's. NOT PROVEN: no attended installed journey -- Henrik has not pressed this himself. The run record above is from a faithful scratch store rather than his live one, because his live store's adopted runner 401s this build's credential; the real store is proven only as far as the control rendering and the command dispatching. FOUND BUT NOT FIXED: the Live output panel read 'Nothing has run yet' in the same frame the snapshot reported one run. EXPECTED CONFLICT AT MERGE: .orchestrate/state.json, append-append, resolve keep-both by JSON union.

THE DECISION: the chief gets a model, and exactly ONE of the two locks MAR-648 recorded moves. broker.handle's first parameter becomes a BrokerPrincipal union ({kind:'agent';agent_id} | {kind:'chief'}) rather than an agent id string -- a type and not a reserved string, because lib/handoff.ts and lib/open-link.ts both accept /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/ and 'dash.fleet' satisfies it, so a string comparison inside the broker would be a hole an agent author could aim at by choosing a name. readManifest answers for the chief with a manifest DASH composes from lib/fleet/catalogue.ts carrying ONE connection and ONE capability ({provider}.chat.completion) -- not a new authority, because ADR 0013 already granted DASH the right to decide what a fleet connection asks for and derived it from the frozen operation table. connectionSecretName DOES NOT MOVE: it goes on emitting dash.connection. and is never called for a chief, which calls fleetSecretName instead, so lib/fleet/principal.ts's sentence -- no agent, named anything at all, resolves to the fleet credential's vault key -- survives verbatim and is now true for two independent reasons. ADR 0013's rejected alternative ('the broker reads the fleet key directly') is amended and scoped to a principal that is not an agent; both its stated reasons were about agents and neither reaches here. NEW INVARIANT: the chief can ask a model a question and be charged for it and can do nothing else. Origin stays 'person' (ADR 0016 untouched, an unattended chief spend is unreachable rather than refused); model is DASH's fleet default with no picker of its own (ADR 0012 decision 4 untouched); the answer still drives nothing. FACTS VS PHRASING, ANSWERED HONESTLY: describeChief's never-reworded rule DOES NOT survive 'which agents run local vs cloud', because that is a join over records and not a quote of one. It is replaced by the briefing rule (every field sent is a string DASH already renders on a screen) plus a receipt rendered from DASH's own records rather than parsed out of the answer -- AskCitation's discipline moved to fleet facts -- plus records-first: answerChief and STANDING_WORDS stay in front, so the most-asked question stays free, instant and exact. What the receipt does NOT prevent is named: a model can still attribute a fact to the wrong agent or drop one, and no test catches that. MEMORY: the session-only argument is answered, not ignored -- it was an argument against undated re-presentation, so the transcript becomes durable (chief_messages beside agent_questions, ADR 0012's own precedent) with the receipt frozen alongside it and a staleness marker computed by comparing two of DASH's own records; the model is told only the last few turns and NEVER an old receipt. No vector store, no embeddings: the chief's memory is conversational continuity, its knowledge is always fresh. VOICE: small talk rides the same call with an empty briefing, never a canned-greeting table, and its receipt says nothing from your records was used. ROOM SCOPE: enforced by the type -- {kind:'chief'} carries no agent id, so no chief question can be aimed at an agent and no agent question can carry the fleet briefing. MODEL RECOMMENDATION: the fleet default, and set it to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001; the consequence that Anthropic does not price its own answers is stated. VISUALS: zero corners HELD. 'Softer' is diagnosed as border count and density, not radius -- .chief-asked's accent bar, .chief-quoted's second rule, .chief-reply at --text-sm so the answer is smaller than the question, and .chief-room a bordered box inside a bordered band. Unbox the turns, return to base size, one accent, keep the square corners. An exception would be a declared one across app/tokens.css and tests/tokens.test.ts and this ADR recommends not spending it yet. SEQUENCING: the boundary, the receipt, the transcript and the visual pass are provable before MAR-647; whether the briefing is ENOUGH, whether phrasing stays faithful, what a question costs, and the hand-off end to end are NOT judgeable until the competitor scout has produced real work -- Henrik's own 'the agents have no real output so we can't really test this'. Station 11 is not closed by this entry.

PLANNED 2026-08-16. MAR-628 slice 1: the controlled browser is built, and ADR 0019 amendment 1 (status proposed, same PR) records what it built against what the ADR's own smallest slice specified. THIS ENTRY IS planned AND PROVES NOTHING BEYOND WHAT IS LISTED UNDER EVIDENCE BELOW.

WHAT SHIPPED. Two operations and no others -- browser.open and browser.read -- in a frozen catalogue lib/browser/operations.ts, pinned BY VALUE in tests/browser-threat-model.test.ts on WRITE_PATHS' terms. BrowserGesture is a union of two members and neither carries a selector, an expression, a key, a coordinate, a frame or a CDP parameter, so no agent can reach Runtime.evaluate: the field an escape would need is not there. Exact HTTPS origins per run from a new manifest block agent_dom.browser, parsed by URL and compared with ===; no prefix match exists anywhere, a path in a declaration is refused rather than silently widened to the host, and every request is checked including subresources and each hop of a redirect chain. One ephemeral WebContentsView per run in an in-memory Electron partition (no persist: prefix, which is the structural reason nothing outlives the run), no preload, sandboxed, popups, downloads, permission prompts, new windows and every non-HTTPS scheme denied. CDP attached by DASH only; the read runs one constant expression in an isolated world, so a page that has redefined its own globals cannot change what DASH reads. Three tables: browser_actions (decisions about requests an agent made), browser_blocked (requests a PAGE made, deliberately with no request id, operation or decision column, on broker_lapses' terms) and browser_sessions (the receipt, whose declared_origins is written once so a manifest edited mid-run cannot change what a finished receipt says). A Stop that destroys the view and refuses the rest of the run, reachable only from DASH's own IPC -- lib/browser/protocol.ts has no stop and no close, so an agent cannot revoke, un-revoke, or notice a revocation except by being refused. Read-then-reach wired: after a successful browser.read, any write or spend for that agent in that run is refused needs_a_person (ADR 0020's rule; its four limits apply unchanged and a fifth, specific to this wiring, is stated on BrowserController.hasReadUntrusted). Its own runner message type, buffer and route pair rather than a widening of the broker's, because a browser request names no connection; BROWSER_ROUTES sits inside LocalRunnerChannel's brand, so calling it on a host's channel is a compile error.

EVIDENCE. pnpm typecheck clean as its own command. brand:check passed. Full suite: 200 files, 3781 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed before the MAR-659 merge, and 203 files / 3828 passed / 11 skipped / 0 failed after it. Four new test files (browser-threat-model, browser-session, browser-read-then-reach, copy-browser) plus updates to the three inventory gates this touches -- shell.test.ts's command list, store-sqlite's migration count, which moved 23 -> 24 and then 24 -> 25 when MAR-659's chief_transcript landed first -- the migration-index collision this project has hit before, caught by the gate that pins the number rather than by an installed store skipping a step, first-paint's exemption list. verify:shell ATTEMPTED AND DID NOT PRODUCE PROOFS, and the reason is recorded rather than assumed: it was run, it reached the installed store, and it died in Chromium cache contention with ZERO proof lines emitted. Three other Electron entry points were live on this machine at the time -- one from the main repo, one from a parallel worktree (dash-mar669), one leftover from this session's own proof runs -- and any lock-holding Electron kills the smoke this way. CI's shell-smoke is therefore the witness for the packaged path, and it PASSED on this branch (run 31967126989), as did verify.

THE REAL RUN. electron/prove-browser.ts drives the real controller against a real page in a real WebContentsView attached to DASH's own window, in a scratch store: 11/11, including a real page loaded (Example Domain), 129 characters of real page text read back through CDP, an origin refusal on https://example.com.attacker.test, a refusal of browser.evaluate, a Stop that destroyed the view and refused afterwards, and the trail read back out of the store. The browser was pixel-aligned with the supervision panel's stage (view and panel both 264,242,688,430), which is the claim ADR 0019 chose Electron over Playwright for.

FOUR DEFECTS THE REAL RUN FOUND AND THIS PR FIXES, none of which any unit test saw. (1) CDP domain-enable at session-open time never settles against a WebContents with no renderer -- every session hung before its first navigation with no error anywhere; domains are enabled lazily and every gesture now has a hard ceiling so a wedged Chromium becomes page_unavailable rather than a blocked agent. (2) The session receipt was written by the drain loop, i.e. the TRANSPORT, so any other caller of handle produced action rows whose session had no row and the whole trail rendered as nothing; it is written by the controller now. (3) An origin refusal happens before a session exists, so it belonged to no session and was written where no person could see it -- the exact failure the trail exists to prevent, arrived at from the other direction; it now renders under 'Refused before anything opened'. (4) browser.viewport's four numbers were denied as missing fields sixteen times per run because required payload keys default to strings, so the browser sat in fallback bounds over the top-left of the window while the panel below it drew an empty stage; payload_types fixes it, on host.create.port's precedent.

WHAT IS DEFERRED AND WHY, in ADR 0019 amendment 1 rather than a commit message: scroll and the approval-required click (they need the approval surface, and building it beside an unproven controller would mean approving gestures against a browser nobody had watched work), typing, forms, uploads, downloads, permissions, multiple tabs, the before-frame, the 'stopping to ASK' half of a cross-origin redirect (the trail says so and the run stops; there is no surface on which a person can widen a run's origins and there should not be one until approval exists), credentials and a persistent profile, and the whole VPS/Xvfb path. The amendment also scores ADR 0019's own eight-point 'full control' checklist honestly: two conditions are VACUOUS because nothing dispatches input, two are not applicable, and condition 8 -- resource use and failure recovery measured under load -- IS NOT MET AND IS THE LARGEST GAP. One concurrent session on one machine has been exercised and nothing here says what several cost. The product therefore continues to say controlled browser operations and not full browser control, and lib/copy/browser.ts contains no sentence with those words in it.

PLANNED 2026-08-16. MAR-673: ADR 0024 (status proposed) -- a decision is filed where it is made, and activity is never filed at all. DOCUMENTATION ONLY. AN ADR PROVES NOTHING; no code exists against this document and nothing moves past planned until Henrik signs it and an implementation slice lands.

WHAT THE ADR PROPOSES, in one paragraph. One new table, fleet_decisions, append-only in the same SQLite store as the records it cites. A decision is a committed change to standing state (agent added/removed, declared-manifest diff on re-import, model pinned/unpinned, fleet default, connection granted/revoked, standing settings, plus a person's approval of an irreversible command), filed at the write-site in the same transaction, kinds frozen in a closed DECISION_KINDS list on WRITE_PATHS' terms. The reason is the person's optional line at decide time or a dash-rule's own copy string, never the model's and never an agent's; absence is stated ('no reason was recorded') and answerable without a model. Staleness is computed at read, twice: supersession by chain key (subject, kind, topic) and a drift marker comparing frozen outcome_json against current state -- which also detects write-sites that failed to file. Retrieval is by subject and complete chain, never keyword or similarity (the scout ask path's 'summarize matched nothing' failure is the named anti-pattern); activity is NEVER filed -- it is projected at ask time from runs/events/run_artifacts/command_audit, because a stored summary is a cached projection that drifts and a speculation cache if a model authors it. The chief reads memory and never writes it, so ADR 0023's blast-radius invariant survives verbatim. Receipts extend chief_messages.receipt_json to a tagged shape (old rows keep reading as fleet rows); every remembered claim names decision rows and record references, and a decisions surface on the fleet page is a prerequisite, not a follow-up, because the briefing rule requires every briefed string to be one DASH renders.

SEQUENCE. Explicitly after ADR 0023's implementation: the memory briefing rides the chief's model call, receipt and transcript, none of which exist as code yet either. The issue's own bar stands: ask the chief something about last week that is true, and get an answer with a receipt naming the records it came from, against a fleet that has actually done something.

ADR 0024 ACCEPTED AND MERGED, 2026-08-16. Henrik signed same-day ('lets sign it and start working'); PR #216 merged to master as 8ec333d with the acceptance recorded in the ADR's own status line. The ADR itself still proves nothing; what follows is the first implementation slice.

SLICE 1 PLANNED, 2026-08-16, branch 000henrik/mar-673-decisions-log-slice1 cut from 8ec333d. THE LOG ITSELF: migration 26 (fleet_decisions, append-only, no FKs on command_audit's stated reason; store-sqlite pins moved 25 -> 26); lib/fleet/decisions.ts (DECISION_KINDS closed list of ten, pinned by value; chainKeyOf on a unit separator; markDecisions computing supersession from ordering and drift from JSON identity between frozen outcome and a current-outcome map, absent-means-did-not-look; declarationDiff turning a re-import into per-declaration drafts, ids not labels so a label rename cannot fire the drift marker); lib/fleet/decisions-store.ts (fileDecision joins the caller's transaction when handed one, warns standalone; readDecisions with projectExchange-style defensive projection -- an unknown kind reads as absence, an unreadable outcome degrades to empty and only disables drift); lib/copy/decisions.ts (every sentence in one module, identifiers as labelled values, NO_REASON_RECORDED as the one sentence for an absent why).

WRITE-SITES WIRED, with the placement lesson learned twice mid-session: filing lives where the DECISION is made, not in shared plumbing. saveAgent files agent_added or the declared diff inside its own transact (old manifest read at the only moment both documents exist); forgetAgent files agent_removed and its cascades (model choice, fleet grants, receipts) deliberately file nothing; model-store files pin/unpin and fleet default set/clear with read-before-write so re-saves are not transitions; connection-actions files per-agent connect/disconnect grants (broker/store.ts recordReceipt/forgetReceipt file NOTHING because shareGrant and withdrawEverywhere fan one decision out to N agents -- a test pins that absence); fleet/store files fleet connect/disconnect on first-insert/actual-delete; fleet/actions files fleet_grant in noteAgentDecision and in adoptFleetCredential only past the MAR-624 repair, so a press whose materialization produced nothing leaves no decision row; agent-dom/runner files irreversible_approval inside the audit transaction, only for allowed+user+irreversible, topic = command id so each press is a chain of one (an approval is an act, and chaining by name would render the first press as 'later changed').

SURFACE: read-only Decisions section on the fleet page (app/_components/fleet-decisions.tsx), drawn from AgentsView.decisions built in the same store read as the cards so a marker cannot disagree with the fleet beside it (chief's own correctness argument); renders the frozen summary, the person's reason quoted or NO_REASON_RECORDED said plainly, 'Later changed, {date}' on superseded rows, the drift sentence in --warn on drifted heads, and 'The latest N of M' when truncated (DECISIONS_PAGE_LIMIT 30, a read limit not retention). Empty log draws nothing. View types defined in lib/views/types.ts (the client boundary) and imported type-only by the builder, so client-bundle's walk reaches no store.

EVIDENCE, all local: pnpm typecheck clean; full vitest suite 204 files, 3854 passed, 9 skipped, 0 failed (fleet-decisions.test.ts 21 tests: pinned kind list, supersession/drift arithmetic, declared diff incl. the Reddit shape, real-store filing through importManifest/forgetAgent/model-store with cascade-files-nothing and same-value-files-nothing both asserted, unknown-kind row reads as absence, and the source tripwire that each named write-site calls fileDecision while broker/store.ts does not; fleet-decisions-render.test.tsx 8 tests: empty log draws nothing, no-reason sentence, quoted late-dated reason, superseded date, drift sentence, truncation note, zero controls). brand:check passed. verify:shell NOT RUN locally -- a parallel session (MAR-654) is live in this working tree and any lock-holding Electron kills the smoke; CI's shell-smoke on the PR is the witness, per the MAR-628 precedent.

DEFERRED TO LATER SLICES, per the ADR's own sequencing: the reasons UI (the optional why line on confirming controls, and annotate-later from the surface -- every slice-1 row files reason null and the surface says so honestly); the chief's memory briefing, receipts extension of chief_messages, and records-first 'no reason was recorded' answers; capture of the surface (listed in the ADR's provable-once-built list; the section is pinned by render test, not yet photographed); step-level overrides, deploy targets and notification routes as kinds (named absent in DECISION_KINDS' own docblock).
