PLANNED, PR OPEN 2026-08-16. ADR 0021's v1 host pack — the SECOND MAR-629 packet; the first (211b73e, PR #185) was the ADR and explicitly proved nothing. Branch 000henrik/mar-629-host-pack, worktree ../dash-mar629-pack, cut from origin/master at a96cfa6 after confirming the tip: the brief named d4552d0 and master had already moved (PR #212, MAR-659), so the brief's commit was stale and is corrected here rather than followed. WHAT LANDED. A ninth deploy verb `pack`, argued in lib/deploy/verbs.ts against ADR 0014's three questions and pinned by value in BOTH by-value pins — tests/deploy-bridge.test.ts and tests/host-record.test.ts — the second of which fired exactly as the brief predicted it would. It is the one verb carrying no identifier at all, and a bundle_id on it is refused rather than ignored. runner/host-pack.ts is ADR 0021 section 3's store on disk: secrets/ 0700, pack.json 0600, wrap.key 0600 (32 bytes, minted once and never re-minted, because re-minting would silently orphan every key already placed and present as a broker refusing a key a receipt says is on the server), keys/{bundle_id}/{connection_id} 0600, AES-256-GCM with the slot as additional authenticated data — so a sealed file moved between bundle directories fails to open rather than being read as that bundle's key, which is what makes the bundle scope isolation rather than a check on a path. POSIX owner/mode proofs run where the platform has them and are skipped on Windows with the skip stated, ADR 0004's shape one directory down; CI is Linux and the host is Linux, so the assertion is real on both machines that matter. runner/host-broker.ts is the second security boundary. It reuses operationById, planCall, the frozen paths, the origins, MAX_MATERIAL_CHARS, MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, aiAuthHeaders and the BrokerRefusal vocabulary — so widening a path stays a reviewed change to the same catalogue and never a host exception — and admits its OWN closed set from lib/broker/host-operations.ts: three suffixes written by value, providers from AI_PROVIDER_IDS, the nine-element product pinned by value in tests/host-broker.test.ts. It is an allow-list and deliberately not a deny-list, because a deny-list naming yesterday's Gmail operations would admit tomorrow's on every enrolled host with no diff anybody read. Gmail and MCP are unknown_operation — the same code an agent gets locally for a name DASH never built, which is ADR 0021 rule 2's vocabulary requirement — and both are refused BEFORE the secrets tree is touched. The host spend allowance is opened by runner/server.ts on the `retry` command only, mirroring electron/main.ts line for line including its ordering argument, with the agent id taken from the URL segment rather than from the unvalidated envelope so one agent's press cannot open another's allowance. runner/supervisor.ts gained ONE optional adjudicator: absent is the local path and nothing about it moves; present is the host, where a request is answered down the pipe it arrived on because ADR 0006 keeps /broker/drain off the remote channel and there is nobody to drain it. Audit rows carry decided_on:'host' on the row rather than at ingest, so a pulled row cannot lose its provenance by being copied; they go to the runner's own log, which `collect` already pulls, rather than to a new route ADR 0021 section 5 forbids. WHAT DID NOT LAND, AND WHY — READ THIS BEFORE THE NEXT SESSION. `install-key` IS NOT IN THIS PACKET. It is ADR 0018's verb and MAR-625's work, and origin/codex/mar-625-key-push (f329bf0, WIP, unmerged) already carries a draft of it touching lib/deploy/verbs.ts and scripts/host-helper/main.ts — the two files this packet also edits — so building it here would have been a guaranteed conflict on a security boundary. This pack ships the STORE that verb writes into (writeHostKey, with the 0700/0600 read-back proof and the refuse-if-the-pack-is-missing rule ADR 0021 requires) and nothing reachable from DASH: no IPC route, no command, no deploy verb. FOR WHOEVER TAKES MAR-625: that WIP writes {root}/secrets/{bundle}/{connection} in PLAINTEXT; ADR 0021 section 3 is later and authoritative, so the layout is {root}/secrets/keys/{bundle}/{connection} sealed under wrap.key, and the verb should call writeHostKey rather than re-implement the write. CONSEQUENTLY MODEL_KEY_STAYS_HOME_REFUSAL IS UNCHANGED AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. 'DASH does not send keys to a server' is still literally true, because no verb sends one. The brief conditioned the gate's exit on 'only once that path truly exists', and it does not yet; writing 'set this host up for AI' now would be a receipt claiming a path that stops one step short — the precise failure ADR 0002 exists to prevent and the one MAR-629's own issue text warns about. lib/copy/host-pack.ts ships the host_pack_too_old sentence instead, which IS reachable today through `pack`, and its docblock records where the missing sentence belongs and what has to be true first. EVIDENCE. pnpm typecheck clean; pnpm brand:check passed; pnpm test 200 files, 3791 passed, 11 skipped, zero failures; pnpm build:runner-standalone green. THE BUILT ARTIFACT WAS DRIVEN, not just compiled: dist/runner-standalone/host-helper.mjs against a fresh DASH_HOST_ROOT answered {"ok":true,"verb":"pack","pack_version":1} and left secrets/{pack.json,wrap.key,keys/} behind with keys/ EMPTY and no {connection_id} file anywhere — ADR 0021 rule 6 executed rather than asserted; runner.mjs carries the host broker; host-helper.mjs contains neither /broker/drain nor /broker/responses. verify:shell NOT RUN and not claimed: Henrik has DASH open, the Electron smoke needs the single-instance lock, and AGENTS.md forbids force-killing it. CI's Windows shell-smoke is this branch's installed witness. NOT PROVEN AND NOT CLAIMED. 186.240.156.166 was not reached — no ssh, no deploy, no status, no bootstrap, no 'just check'. No key has crossed to any host. No agent has thought on a server. No provider was contacted; the one substitution in tests/host-broker.test.ts is fetchImpl, which is what lets the planted-key assertion be made from outside. ADR 0018's substrate stays 'the key is on that server', never 'your agent can now think there'. MAR-489's attended run is what changes that, and it needs Henrik at the machine.

issues.note: PLANNED, NOT MERGED AND NOT PROVEN: branch 000henrik/mar-676-store-reconciliation cut from origin/master d346c7e (confirmed master's tip before the cut). THREE DEFECTS, ALL THREE BUILT. (1) THE RECONCILIATION, in lib/store-reconcile.ts, run by migrate() before it reads user_version -- it has to be before, because it changes that number. Signature: user_version in 24..26, the multi-account shape present (account_id on fleet_connections AND fleet_account_assignments exists), and at least one of master's 24-26 tables absent. No commit of master produces that combination at any version, which is the whole argument for recognising it by shape. On it: copy dash.sqlite + -wal + -shm beside themselves as dash.sqlite.before-reconcile-<ISO stamp>[-wal|-shm] on retireDamagedStore's conventions (all three or none, the marker before the sibling suffix so a recovery tool finds the log, never a subdirectory, COPYFILE_EXCL so a collision refuses instead of overwriting); run MIGRATIONS[23..25] -- the steps themselves, sliced by the caller, so this module holds no copy of their SQL; create any of migration 27's three declared indexes that is missing; run 27's own DELETE of the superseded dash.fleet connection_secrets row; set user_version to 27 in the same transaction. AN INDEX MISTAKE WAS CAUGHT BY THE TESTS AND IS WORTH RECORDING: the first draft sliced MIGRATIONS at 24 because tests/store-sqlite.test.ts' version pin numbers steps by the user_version they PRODUCE, and an index into that array is one less -- so it created the browser tables and the decisions log and silently left chief_messages out, which is the original defect reproduced by the code written to fix it. The repair now verifies inside the transaction that every table it reported creating exists, and rolls back with a named message if not. WHAT IT REFUSES: any column, primary key, secret_name uniqueness or is_default CHECK difference from migration 27, an index present with different columns/uniqueness/partiality, and a fleet_connections_v% table left by a replacement that did not finish. A refusal throws, DASH does not start, the shape check runs BEFORE the backup so nothing is written, and the message prints the whole shape it found so one attempt yields the answer instead of another guess. EXPECTED_FLEET_SHAPE is pinned against a real freshly-migrated store by a test, so a change to migration 27 fails there rather than as a refusal on somebody's machine. db() now closes the handle when migrate() throws; before this a failed open leaked an unreachable open database that on Windows also held its own directory. (2) STANDING READS THE VAULT. FleetConnectorView.held gains secret_readable (drives the chip) and unreadable (the sentence, composed where the vault label is known); both are set together by withFleetSecretStandings in lib/fleet/secret-read.ts, which the IPC read channel runs -- view.connections is now async. The decorator follows the row's secret_name into the vault, returns only whether the read succeeded, and puts neither the name nor the value on the view (asserted). lib/views/build.ts defaults secret_readable to FALSE, deliberately: a default of true would let any path that skips the decoration claim a read it never made. lib/copy/fleet-standing.ts owns the decision and the words: fleetStanding says connected only when the secret resolves, unreadable gets its own amber chip 'DASH cannot read this', and describeFleetSecretUnreadable is now the single author of the sentence Henrik read -- shareFleetConnection calls it and appends only 'Nothing was given out.', so two of the three disagreeing surfaces now say the same words. BOTH CHIP RENDERERS were changed: app/_components/fleet-connector.tsx and chipOf in lib/connections-list.ts each had their own two lines deriving 'connected' from held !== null, which is how they could disagree. The MAR-643 capture scene now writes the two vault entries its rows point at; without them it was seeding Henrik's broken state and would have photographed the honest failed chip. (3) THE WORKTREE GUARD, decided rather than patched: foreignCheckoutProblem in lib/shell/app-identity.ts refuses the installed userData when the app path is neither the packaged app nor the MAIN git working tree, distinguished by whether <app path>/.git is a directory (main) or a file holding gitdir: (linked worktree) -- git's own distinction, one statSync, no marker file to create or remember. DASH_ALLOW_INSTALLED_STORE=1 is the explicit opt-in and the refusal names all three remedies. Gated on isAppEntryPoint, the same question app.setName asks, so the smoke and a dozen capture harnesses launched as a FILE are outside it by construction -- MAR-424's third criterion needs the smoke on the real user-data directory. THE RESIDUAL HOLE IS NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the smoke still opens the real installed store from a worktree, so `pnpm verify:shell` in a worktree remains a write to Henrik's store, and that is very likely the mechanism that produced MAR-676 in the first place -- a `pnpm verify` from dash-mar643 is a far more ordinary act than a manual `electron .`. Closing it means changing what that proof is about and is a separate decision. A CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE'S DIAGNOSIS: the OpenRouter credential is NOT gone. DASH does not use Windows Credential Manager as a store -- lib/vault.ts keeps one safeStorage-encrypted file per secret under <userData>/vault and only LABELS the backing 'Windows Credential Manager (DPAPI)'. dash-secret-dash.fleet.openrouter.api_key.enc is present, 393 bytes, created 2026-08-10T20:02:17.642Z, format_version 1, backend os_keychain, with 288 characters of intact base64 ciphertext. So the envelope parses and get() reaches decryptString, which means the failure is vault_locked and not not_found, and the honest copy says the key is still there rather than telling somebody to re-enter one -- which lib/vault.ts refuses to risk because doing it overwrites the good one. Henrik re-pasting remains his call and is harmless; it is no longer established as necessary. NOT DONE: no ADR (nothing here is cross-repository, and a new ADR number is the one thing parallel packets reliably collide on); the store's own diverged shape was NOT read from Henrik's file -- a copy to scratch was declined by the permission classifier, so the repair verifies the shape at boot instead and prints what it finds. issues.note: PLANNED, NOT MERGED AND NOT PROVEN: branch 000henrik/mar-678-quit-hang cut from master 234e50c. THE CAUSE IS NOT ANY OF THE FOUR SUSPECTS THE ISSUE LISTED -- not closeDb's checkpoint, not the broker stop, not a child refusing shutdown, not a vault call. THE QUIT CHAIN NEVER STARTED. app.quit() is only ever called from window-all-closed, and window-all-closed counts OPEN windows, hidden or not. electron/approval-popup.ts hides its window rather than closing it when nothing is pending, and its own docblock stated the invariant that caused this ('the window is never destroyed while DASH runs'). So any session in which one approval was ever pending and then decided left a hidden window Electron was still waiting on: the user closes DASH, the main window is destroyed, the popup is not, window-all-closed never fires, and before-quit/will-quit -- and therefore closeDb's checkpoint -- never run. The process lives on windowless, holding the store, until Windows is restarted. LIVE FORENSICS CONFIRMED IT BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN, on the survivor MAR-678 itself names: PID 7572 was still running from the 14:00 boot, and an EnumWindows sweep of that PID (read-only, no store access) found exactly one Chrome_WidgetWin_1 -- invisible, titled OrchestrateDASH, which lib/shell/preflight.ts's RENDERER_TITLE makes the title of every DASH page -- beside its GPU, network-utility, detached runner and ONE renderer child created at 15:02:11, an hour after the process started. A window that was never destroyed, and a renderer far younger than the boot: the popup, created when an approval arrived late in the session. THE FIX IS ONE LINE PLUS TWO GUARDS. (1) createWindow's 'closed' handler now calls closeApprovalPopup() -- nothing of DASH's may outlive the window the user closed; before-quit still calls it too, for a quit that starts from the menu or the OS. (2) lib/shell/shutdown.ts runs before-quit's five steps and will-quit's one inside per-step boundaries, because those are event listeners: a throw comes back out of app.quit() and the quit simply does not happen, which reproduces the identical windowless survivor from any failure in the broker stop, the browser teardown, a safeStorage call or a store another process has locked. Failures are named on the shell log and the sequence always reaches its end. (3) A 5s deadline armed when the app window closes (never on darwin, where window-all-closed does not quit either) attempts the checkpoint and then app.exit(0), logging which windows were still open -- so the NEXT window that makes this happen is named in one line instead of found by enumerating HWNDs of a process nobody may kill. A healthy quit measures ~13ms, so the deadline is ~400x the observed cost. MAR-415 IS UNTOUCHED AND WAS RE-CHECKED: the detached runner is not torn down by any of this; the quit path never touched it and still does not. NON-GOALS HELD: no change to when the popup appears or what it shows, no change to the notifier's tick, no ADR, no migration, lib/db.ts NOT TOUCHED (closeDb needed no change -- it was never the blocker). electron/prove-quit.ts is new and permanent, on electron/prove-start.ts's exact terms (evidence not a gate, named by no package.json script, its own DASH_DATA_DIR required rather than defaulted), and it is registered in scripts/build-shell.mjs and electron/README.md. issues.note: PLANNED, NOT MERGED AND NOT PROVEN. RESEARCH ONLY - this issue was a research and decision anchor and this packet entry records a finding, not a build. VERDICT: the gap is DASH's and it is structural, in three places - the broker operation vocabulary (digest.curate returns at most an overview plus twelve label/summary pairs and has no field an author could use to ask for prose; chat.completion's own system prompt forbids markdown, headings, bullets and links), the run-artifact contract (kind admits digest|draft, a digest is items[] plus optional curation{}, and there is no member a written briefing could live in), and the renderer (digest.tsx draws every item with no cap, by design, because nothing collected may be hidden). No plan can produce a newsletter today because no operation writes one, no field carries one and no component draws one. THE PREMISE IN THE ISSUE IS WRONG IN A WAY THAT STRENGTHENS THE FINDING: the scout was not built by the MCP. Its provenance is create-dash-agent 0.1.1 (DASH's own agent-kit) plus hand-writing, with plan_source composed and playbook_id and route_id both empty. So the run Henrik read is the best case - an expert-authored agent with the MCP removed - and it still produced a roundup, which isolates DASH as the binding constraint. ONE STRAIGHT BUG FOUND: deep_dive.text is the only prose the scout ever holds and DASH's renderer drops it. deep_dive is absent from run-artifact.schema.json, from DigestArtifact and from every component; it survives only because additionalProperties is open. It is rendered exclusively in the saved markdown file behind the high-risk gate, and the manifest's own gate copy - 'Saying no loses nothing: the same briefing is already on this page' - is therefore false whenever a deep dive was written. THE MCP IS BROKEN BEHIND THAT WALL, AND WORSE THAN THE ISSUE ASSUMES: it emits AI capability ids as `${provider}.${component_id}`, which operationById does not resolve, so execute.ts answers unknown_operation and every model step of an MCP-authored agent is refused before it reaches a provider. Its pinned copy of DASH's manifest schema still says access is read|write where DASH has admitted spend since MAR-619, and exportBuildBrief.ts:2816 has no spend branch at all, so a frontier step that charges the account is emitted as read. It holds no copy of run-artifact.schema.json and no reference to the artifact channel, and its default panel binds no artifact role. Its component vocabulary and the scout's share not one id, and because component_id binds nothing on either side no gate in either repo can see the disagreement. ASKED TO PLAN THE SCOUT'S OWN GOAL VERBATIM, the live MCP returned a candidate route with coverage 'poor': page_monitor (recommending a paid Firecrawl connection for Atom feeds fetch() reads unauthenticated), job_queue, research_synthesis, citation_checker (which verifies LLM-generated citations, a failure DASH's index-only projection makes unrepresentable), source_freshness_check, state_store - with no approval gate, and with the DASH Agent Runner as an alternative rather than the recommendation. The one thing it gets right is research_synthesis, whose registry entry specifies exactly the operation DASH does not have. RECOMMENDATION, DASH FIRST: D1 draw the deep dive or correct the gate copy (small, a bug); D2 a compose operation whose projection binds prose to items by index, preserving the citation property (ADR-worthy); D3 an artifact shape to carry it; D4 a renderer that leads with the document and folds the list without hiding it, applied in BOTH outputs.tsx and panel.tsx. THEN THE MCP: M1 re-sync dashBrokerCatalog.ts and the broker fixture and add the operation catalogue with access classes, with a drift check like the one agent.manifest.v2.schema.json already has - this is the highest-priority MCP item and is not about output at all; M2 add spend to emitter and schema; M3 teach it the artifact contract, which depends on D2/D3 existing first; M4 a validated DASH route in the registry. NOT DONE AND NAMED IN THE DOCUMENT: export_build_brief was not called and no MCP-authored manifest was imported into DASH, so the unknown_operation prediction is reasoned from source rather than observed. The cheapest next proof is to author one agent through plan_workflow -> export_build_brief -> an LLM and import it, to find out how many steps in the pipeline fails. On this evidence the answer is one: the first model call.
